title: Moldy rat hole with lousy breakfast and unprofessional staff
body: It was a lousy moldy rat hole. We made a mistake picking up the hotel that seemed to have such a nice location. The nearly 400€ per night we paid was a total dissappointment. The staff who actually could of made our stay a bit better, was unprofessional and seemed like they didn’t care. You will not get good mornings wished here. The receptionist said ”ok” and just took the key cards when we checked out. No thank you for staying here, safe trip home or wish you had nice time. Nothing. They were lurking and hiding behind the reception desk every time we went by. At the breakfast the only fresh thing was sliced cucumber and violently cutted tomatoes. At least give the breakfast staff that seemed so miserable, a sharp knife. Canned fruits and sugary sh*t. Lousy and cheap. Where was the bacon?! The breakfast room in the basement had such a bad air. Stairways smelled like mold. Room doors loudly slammed and the carpet in the room was stale and nasty. Would not recommend to anyone.

title: Do not recommend
body: We expect hotel rooms in Europe to be small, but this was exceptionally small. The bathroom was smaller than that on a cruise ship. When we first walked in, the room smelled like stinky feet and was very hot. It seems like the carpet had not been cleaned in a while. Then we realized there was no air-conditioning. So we opened the windows and got out the oscillating fan that was provided. Trying to sleep was difficult, as the road noise outside was very loud we had to have the window open due to the temperature. There was no screen, so we took our chances on bugs and pigeons coming in. Breakfast was not impressive. The fruit provided was canned. Orange juice was like Tang. Be prepared to carry your suitcases up the stairs to the hotel front door and then also down some stairs to get to the lift. Front desk staff was minimally helpful. I think there might’ve been a language barrier. The taxi service they ordered for us one morning, match the quality of the hotel. The car was not even marked as a taxi,so when my husband went to look in the car window and found the guy asleep, he figured it wasn’t our driver. So we waited an additional 10 minutes before the man got out of his car to come and find us.

title: Too hot
body: The hotel was nice, the room beautiful and clean with the essentials; it was cleaned every morning and the sheets and towels were always changed. Only 2 things were not the best: 1, the staff was very unpleasant and rude, but this was not a big problem. The real problem was the heat; I even had to take 4 showers a day because of how much I was sweating, even after the shower just sitting there I was sweating, in the evening my sheets were damp and even with the fan on high it was too hot. I recommend installing an air conditioner.

title: Superb location, great staff, rooms needs upgraded aircon/fan set-up
body: Reception staff day and night were very friendly and helpful , first impressions excellent The room was spotlessly clean. One small thing - the clingy shower curtains should really be phased out, The main area in need of overhaul is the fan situation. I appreciate that in older building such as this that fitting modern air-con is no easy job however ceiling mounted fans would be a huge improvement. Currently desktop small plastic fans are available in the rooms. Given the weather conditions this summer and the likelihood of this weather occurring more regularly in northern Europe this is an area of concern The location is excellent, close to public transport in an area that feels safe at night and has that old fashioned London tree-lined feel, no noise issues. There is a small friendly bar, although not sure of hours of operation.

title: THERE IS NO AC AND WINDOWS DO NOT OPEN
body: I booked this hotel on a whim when I had a 24 hour layover in London. I chose this hotel because of its location, but I was here during the heat wave when it was over 90 degrees - so you can imagine my shock when I got to my room and realized not only is there no AC, the windows do not open to allow any breeze. It was cooler outside where it was 90 degrees than in my room! Thankfully, Expedia refunded me and I checked into The Byron Hotel just down the street that DID have AC. Overall, this hotel is in a great location and is probably fine when it’s cooler, but I definitely would not recommend staying here in the summer. 1 star since I literally could not stay here due to the heat.

title: Absolutely disgusting service. Never again.
body: I rarely leave reviews, but my experience here was so unprofessional I feel others should be warned. At checkout I was handed a card by reception clearly marked “Continental Breakfast” and told to show it to staff downstairs. On that basis, I entered the breakfast area. While eating, a staff member asked for the card (which should have been checked before entry). Minutes later she returned, and in front of surrounding tables loudly announced that breakfast was not included in my room. I was left with food in my mouth while other guests stared in silence — a humiliating and completely unnecessary scene. As a paying guest, I should never have been treated like a thief. If clarification was needed, it could and should have been handled discreetly. I would have happily paid for breakfast, but the way this was done was degrading and ruined my stay. I raised this formally with management, giving them the chance to resolve it, but they ignored and dismissed my concerns — which says everything about their attitude toward guests. On top of that, the room had no air conditioning and was uncomfortably hot. The only positive is the area itself — central, with plenty of other hotels nearby. My advice: choose one of the many alternatives in the area where professionalism and basic respect for guests is standard.

title: Reasonable
body: Exterior of the hotel looked in need of renovation compared to other old Victorian mansions nearby, Wall had some cracks and dents also the rails with nails around the edges of the outside of the hotel was also not a nice sight. Inside against that it was clean and nicely dressed and the reception friendly and helpful, also it was nice that before I could go to my room my roll suitcase could be left there secured. Room was fine at first glance but when I came into the bathroom and especially the shower I really thought of yaks. There was mild mold on the shower head, shower tray was more brown than white due to rust and are small pieces loose and non-slip mat was still wet and at the bottom was still hair of the previous occupant anvil stuck (it was not me bald). This was reported and was listened to neatly and got another room (were surprised that it was dirty mudflats because they clean well they say) New room was clean and tidy so I mudflats happy but because I had 1 single room I got a small 1 person bed where I can sleep on a kind of roll meganism to move around more easily in the room. Bed was basically fine but was not comfortable and because of the heats I pulled the molton and fitted lacquer from the mattress often slept briefly everywhere. Before the heats they had a fan in the room that we helped but when coming out of the field of the fan you felt the smell of heat, something the hotel can not do anything about. Breakfast was simple and good and for extra costs you could ask for special breakfast such as English breakfast which in my opinion did not correspond to the price 7 pounds and 50 penc. In short for a 3 star hotel I think they leave some stitches but for a 2 star class it is more in the mindset.

title: Terrible Customer Service
body: The blonde hair girl working the front desk has terrible customer service skills even for London standards. I was checking in and she was so unwelcoming and bitter like I just ran over her dog or something. As for the room I was given, it was small. A single bed with uncomfortable pillows and the room was about 7 feet wide. The breakfast provided is continental. It had a good selection but in the end it is continental so no hot items are available. I have stayed in central London many times and for this price range there are better options available with larger rooms, a hot breakfast, and better customer service. I wouldn't return to this hotel.

title: Absurdedly small room
body: I had a so-called triple family room. While it did have 3 beds, 2 of them were pushed together and there was about a foot of room on either side of the beds and about a foot in front. No room to place a suitcase, no room to stretch, no room to sit, and barely any room to walk - if you wanted to pass, you had to hop on the bed. Ridiculous. Was just myself and my 2 teen children, and fortunately we were out most of the days, but when you want to come to your room, you want some space, not a glorified closet. On top of that, the floors squeaked horribly, so any movement at all triggered the old haunted house noise. For the amount of money we paid, this was an absolutely disappointing hotel. I'll give it 2 stars for a quiet location near a metro.

title: Good Value - Good Location
body: My wife and I stayed for two nights at Hotel Phoenix on Sept 12, 2024. Upon arrival at around 4pm, we found the greeting by front desk staff to be unenthusiastic and indifferent, which made for a poor first impression. However the room was quite adequate. Small but clean. The location is great for making nearby underground connections to Paddington and other city stations. Though there's lots of nearby shopping, the street in front of the hotel was very quiet making for a peaceful sleep. The surprise for us was the large breakfast room which was well stocked, and quite popular.

body: Hotel was in a great location, not far from tube and pubs and restaurants. Staff were also very friendly, that's where the positive ends. We were given a below ground room which no air con. It was probably the hottest weekend of the year so we had to leave the window open (bars on the window so felt safe enough) but could still hear noise from outside. The pillows were very lumpy and uncomfortable, combined with the heat we didn't get much sleep. On our second day we went down for continental breakfast to be greeted by the coffee machine not switched on and mouldy bread.

title: A nice hotel in a good location
body: As a couple, we spent two nights at this hotel in April. First of all, the location is really ideal. Very close to the metro, a shopping street and in a quiet area. The entrance is very pretty and the welcome was pleasant. We had a room on the top floor. The room was very small but functional and pretty. On the other hand, it was very hot even though the outside temperatures were average and there was no air conditioning (just a fan). I don't recommend going there in the middle of summer, it must be unbearable. The choice was limited for breakfast and we really didn't find it appetizing.

title: Average
body: This was a perfectly fine experience at a budget hotel. The staff was pleasant and the location was convenient. The (single) room was incredibly small, smaller than the photos imply, and there was nowhere to store my suitcase. I found it strange that the staff didn't replace coffee cups (instant coffee and kettle was provided) or answer the phone at reception. Also, my suitcase was delivered after me and the woman at the reception desk said it wasn't! It wasn't until I showed her the airtag tracker that she went back to check and located it. I plan to spend a little more and stay somewhere else next trip.

body: Second stay here. Rooms here are tiny. I booked a standard double they gave me a single bed room that I could touch all 4 walls from the bed. When I complained they made it my problem and told me to contact Agoda . Horrible customer service. Finally they gave me the room I booked which was bigger but still tiny. Last visit I stayed in an executive room which is passable but very small. Breakfast is very average. The whole place is serviced by one lift from the 1950s which means you are constantly waiting. Look it's cheap. The area is decent. But I'm not coming back. I can't recommend.

title: Good hotel close to station but...
body: The hotel itself is close to the subway station, has been renovated, and has a lift, so even with large luggage I was able to get to my room without any problems. There are several supermarkets nearby, and although I didn't use them, there were also a few pubs. Personally, it was helpful that there was a coin laundry about a 10-minute walk away. However, it is not open late like in Japan, so you need to be careful about the time you use it. The problem was that I was infested with what appeared to be bedbugs. I didn't tell the hotel because there was no physical evidence, but the itching did not stop for about two weeks afterwards. I recommend checking the bed and ventilating the room.

However, it is not open late like in Japan, so you need to be careful about the time you use it. The problem was that I was infested with what appeared to be bedbugs. I didn't tell the hotel because there was no physical evidence, but the itching did not stop for about two weeks afterwards. I recommend checking the bed and ventilating the room.

title: Not our old Phoenix anymore, what a pity and goodbye!
body: Unfortunately, the Phoenix Hotel has declined considerably. But it is getting more and more expensive. While a room on the hotel's own website cost around £50 in 2022, it is now usually three to four times as much. But there is a big problem with the window, which is leaky and therefore drafty, and the heating, which cannot be regulated via a thermostat. So it is essentially always very cold or very hot. So our stay at the Phoenix Hotel this year, after almost 25 years, will definitely be the last for a very long time. I don't think we will be coming back. Definitely not.

title: Great location, employee Inês is excellent
body: Friendly hotel, very well located, in a calm and safe neighborhood, with many restaurants, supermarkets and cafes, and close to the metro, buses and parks. I highlight the extreme attention and friendliness of Mrs. Inês, who was working in the breakfast area, and was super loving with us. The twin room is great. The negative points are: - Family room is small at maximum capacity - 4 people; - The bathroom should have a shower, instead of a bathtub, which is highly discouraged for children or elderly guests or those with reduced mobility; - Corridors leading to the rooms are very narrow - in an emergency situation it would certainly go wrong; - The elevator doesn't always work, but we ended up always using the stairs, which is actually good for us :); - Breakfast is very limited in terms of options - there is no fresh fruit, for example; - The breakfast room is small for the hotel's capacity, every time we arrived, once at 8.30 and the other at 9.00, there was never a table available. Thanks :)

title: Bed size warning!
body: Americans take note! I booked an "executive double" room, stated to be a larger room with a KING bed. Turns out it is really a queen by American standards. The photo on the website is VERY misleading, making both the bed and room look much larger than they really are. We would have been better off booking a twin room - the bed space would have been bigger and added up to a true king size bed. I complained at the front desk when we arrived and was told "Madam, that is the largest bed we have". We would have been far more comfortable if they had moved us to a twin room. Breakfast was OK, nothing special and the coffee was always cold.

title: Poor and won't return
body: This was disappointing. We paid over £200 for a 1 night stay and to be honest, it was a rip-off. The double room we had was OK but the bathroom is a disaster waiting to happen. There is a raised threshold to go into the bathroom. If you use the facilities in the night or at any other time you are likely to trip. Then the shower is over the bath. The problem here is the toilet is too close to the bath which leaves an inadequate space to enter the bath. As a result, I slipped, banged my knee badly as I lost my balance. There is also no grab rail to hold onto once you finish. If the bath was replaced with a shower, then it wouldn't be a problem. I was also disappointed with the continental breakfast. OK, it's continental but all that was on offer was boiled eggs, rolls, croissants, tinned fruit and cold meat which was curling up at the sides indicating that 'it was on the turn'. The table was also dirty, and we had to ask for it yo be cleaned, and for some coffee cups. Very poor, and to be honest, I've had much better continental breakfasts elsewhere. At £225 for one night, we feel short changed by the whole place. The only decent thing is that for London, the area is reasonably quiet and the overall cleanliness of the hotel is decent, but we won't be returning.

title: What do you mean you don't have a room..?
body: We were looking forward to our stay in London. We traveled to Iceland, then Dublin, and our last stop was London. The Phoenix Hotel was the only hotel during our trip that had a family room available. We were looking forward to staying, at last, all in the same room. That changed quickly when we checked into the Phoenix hotel and got to our room. It was a triple that they put a cot in. The room had a loft and at the top of the stairs is where the cot was placed...so if you got out of bed...down the stairs you would went..not good. They had no other rooms available. We were told that they couldn't be responsible for the issue since we booked through q travel agent (huh?). We booked over a year ago...and we have confirmation for a quad...what more can I say. We spent the next 2 hours looking for another hotel..

title: Great room configuration
body: I stayed there with my daughter & grandson. The room was great because my grandson had his own private area. Great location to get on the Tube & to the park. Staff were mainly helpful. Breakfast was poor in my opinion only tinned fruit & mass produced packaged items. Extra was charged for items that are normally served for breakfast in hotels of the same standard. A taxi was called by the staff for me, which didn’t arrive (not the receptions fault) however their inability to deal with the matter was very stressful. Luckily a guest helped me & I didn’t miss my train but only by seconds. The most stressful experience. I would strongly suggest that the hotel use a more reliable taxi service for its customers. I’m undecided if I’d stay there again although it does have a lot of advantages.

title: Noisy
body: Stayed here for 1 night for business, upon arrival the hotel provided a voucher for a free drink at the bar as a reward for being an Expedia Gold member. Very nice welcome touch! My room was on the ground floor and facing the front street, which was very loud. I asked reception if they had an alternate room, but sadly nothing was available. Sadly the room was very loud, and I had to sleep with the TV on to block out the noise of cars, passers by pulling cases along the tarmac and people talking right outside my window. This room should really have double glazing to reduce the sound, as it’s really not suitable at current. Overall the room was very clean, spacious - the bathroom was very small but suitable for a 1 night business trip. Would recommend for business travellers but bathroom would be extremely small for more than 1 person sharing the room.

Sadly the room was very loud, and I had to sleep with the TV on to block out the noise of cars, passers by pulling cases along the tarmac and people talking right outside my window. This room should really have double glazing to reduce the sound, as it’s really not suitable at current. Overall the room was very clean, spacious - the bathroom was very small but suitable for a 1 night business trip. Would recommend for business travellers but bathroom would be extremely small for more than 1 person sharing the room.

title: Disappointing
body: Check-in was horrible. The young woman who tried to check me in wanted to confirm whether I was at the correct hotel. I am not sure she actually understood English (she was definitely not a native English speaker) She then could not find my booking (not able to find my surname). I was then not provided information regarding where breakfast would be served. I went down to breakfast the next morning and the wait staff did not even offer me tea or coffee. The wait staff did not even greet me or acknowledge me. This was disgusting as I had stayed at this hotel two weeks ago and the service level had definitely declined to an unacceptable level. The evening was extremely noisy and at midnight, there were people talking loudly near my room. There were no staff members or managers to ensure that the noise level was kept to a minimum.

title: Very disappointing
body: Good reception staff but that's where the good things stopped. Had paid in advance for a twin bed room but was given a room that was nothing more than a broom cupboard. A single bed that was jammed up against a wall and less than a foot to the next wall. I assumed for a minute that the bathroom was a cupboard it was that small. Window jammed open and the heater going flat out. Breakfast was really strange with not much in the way of choice, but the way it was set out was bizarre. Lift was so antiquated it felt like it was always about to fail. Location was OK and it seemed popular with visiting Germans and Australians, but the hotel failed in so many ways it was laughable. A decent room might make it livable, but as far as I was concerned I would never stay there again.

title: Okay, but not great
body: This hotel was booked for me by a tour group. Because London was an add-on after my Scotland tour, I rather wish I had booked my own hotel in London. Here are the plusses; the staff here is very friendly and helpful, the rooms are small, but clean and pretty well appointed. There are nice sitting areas and a bar right at the front of the hotel. Nice place to hang and have a drink after running around the city all day. Despite being off a busy street (Queensway), the hotel's location is very quiet. You're also a short walk away from Kensington Park/Kensington Palace area, which is a nice place to walk through. The minuses; the smaller rooms have twin/single beds, which were as hard as a rock. I have back issues, but my travelling companion doesn't and even she complained about backaches and poor sleep from the too firm mattress and pillows. The breakfast offerings were rather bland.The Queensway street area is a rather cheap area, with mediocre restuarants and tacky souvenir shops. You would need to take a taxi or bus to get anywhere with better places to eat and shop. (We got tour bus passes that came out close to where the hotel is located, but, alas, they didn't run very late.) Despite some good parts to the hotel, the uncomfortable beds and the location would give me pause about staying here again.

title: Make sure you get the room you have booked!
body: I stayed here for 3 nights last month and booked the executive double room - the largest room offered, after reading reviews about the small sized rooms ( which is understandable in the city). I didn't play much attention to the room when I first checked in as I had to go straight back out but when I got back I realized that room was actually really small and looked nothing like the pictures of the executive double. It looked just liked the standard double room, I questioned this with reception and asked them to confirm the room type I was in, but they couldn't tell me and said the would have to check with the manager in the morning ( odd- I work on a hotel front desk and know what all the room types are so not sure why they had to check with the manager to find out what room type I was in! ). In the morning the manager confirmed I was in the right room - strange how it looked nothing like the pictures and very small! - in the end they offered to move me to an 'upgraded room' of a queen executive - strange this room type does not seem to exist on their website or anywhere else! Once I got the new room, it looked exactly like the room I was expecting and it was very nice, shame I didn't get it to begin with as otherwise I would have not had any issues with the hotel and would recommend it. They did refund me the difference of the two rooms for the first night after emailing them once I departed. Do note the rooms get very hot, even though it was winter, I still had to sleep with the windows open all night, so I wouldn't recommend this hotel in the summer,

title: A very disappointing hotel.
body: I went to this hotel because of recommendations on Trip Advisor and was VERY disappointed. It's reasonably clean and well kept up. The rooms are small, which is OK, because the price is very moderate. BUT two major problems:. I kept getting awakened by people walking overhead. Any kind of noise was magnified The floors creaked like a haunted house. And the room was very warm, and there was no thermostat to regulate the heat, even though it was in 50s outside. I woke up sweating. I finally kept the window open. Basically, I had a lot of trouble getting a good night's sleep at this hotel, and that's the single most important thing I look for in a hotel.

body: I’ve been visiting London for the first time, and I was advised by a close friend of mine, experienced in visiting this city, to stay in the Paddington area. And she was right. If you are flying to and from Heathrow, I highly recommend booking Heathrow express tickets, they will commute you from LHR terminal 5 to Paddington station in only 25 mins, same trip duration on the way back to the airport. From Paddington to the Phoenix Hotel, prepare to immerse yourself in the overcomplicated network of the London underground aka tube. I recommend using Bayswater station (district and circle lines) if you are travelling with baggage. If not, in my experience, Queensway tube station is very close too and connects you better to the touristic places through the central line, which is one of the underground lines that remains open Friday and Saturday nights. Location: the hotel it’s in Kensington gardens square, between the areas of Paddington and the rest of Kensington and Chelsea, rather posh areas in tfl zone 1, the hotel 1-2 mins on foot away from Queensway, a commercial street with restaurants, prêt-à-manger, souvenirs shops, phone shops, Tesco, Boots and an upmarket shopping centre (Whitley’s), 3-4 mins away from Bayswater tube station and 6-7 mins away from Queensway tube station; and 8 mins away on foot to famous Hyde Park. Of course, there are many good areas in London in which to pick a hotel, but I think this is one of the best. By the way, the façade of the hotel is beautiful. Rooms: I can state I was very satisfied with the room I was assigned. The responsible staff took into due consideration my request for a bed in which a very tall man like me could fit, and they satisfied my expectations. I loved the bed and the room. The bathroom was nice as well, the only inconvenience was that it was hard to regulate the water temperature, so most of my showers were hotter than I wished for. The staff, once again, was friendly and a lady from the cleaning staff helped me regulate the temperature once. The cleaning service was good. Of course, all hotel rooms and showers are small in European capitals whose main industry is not tourism and hospitality, but in my case, I had all the personal space I needed. Unfortunately, they do not have magnetic cards as keys, so you have to carry around a heavy metal key or leave it in the reception and ask for it to get back in the room when you return to the hotel. I got views to backyard, quiet, no problems. I don't know if any other bedrooms like mine had better views on the front façade. Breakfast: I found it interesting that there was always a member of staff making sure there was enough toasted bread for the guests, that’s a detail I appreciated. There wasn’t a lot of variety, and the juices had too much sugar. Staff will ask you when you first sit down if you want hot water and tea, or coffee, or cool milk, etc. I think one of the two only things the hotel needs to improve is the food variety. The other improvement would be to substitute old-fashioned metal keys for magnetic cards, easier to handle and use. Staff: they were nice, they will give you a hand when needed, you can talk to them for tourist advice or just to chat a bit if you are travelling solo, like in my case. Overall, it is a hotel I would recommend to stay in. Definitely, it would be a pleasure for me to come back, provided they let me stay in the same room I stayed.

title: Nice hotel but no air conditioning
body: This seems like a nice hotel, but if you are traveling in the summer, make sure you know that there is no air conditioning. The temperature in our room was over 100 and after having the window open and fans running all night, it had "cooled" down to 87 in the morning. The only rooms that might be an option is if they are on a lower level and not facing the south. We stayed one night and then switched to another hotel that had air conditioning. I would avoid this hotel from June though August.

title: Good location, but that’s it
body: I stayed here for one night while in London. I was able to leave my bag here for the day as my room was not available an hour before check in. When I came back to check in much later, they could not find my luggage. I tried not to lose my temper, and luckily my bag was safely in my room even though the employee said it’s issued just in the back. The room itself was loud, hot, and not clean. I booked a single room, with one bed, yet I received a triple room with three single beds. It was an L shaped room, and one bed was directly under the window in the room. I was on the ground floor & the window was open. It was directly on the ground level and people walked by outside all night and kept waking me up. I did not actually feel safe being at that level so close to the street with no real security around the window. There was no air conditioning and the room was very hot so I could not close the window. There were stains on the white duvets, and on the carpet as well. The one good thing about the room was the good water pressure in the shower. I would not stay here again, as even though the location was good, there are endless options in the same area or others for the same or better prices.

I would not stay here again, as even though the location was good, there are endless options in the same area or others for the same or better prices.

title: Nice Hotel and Great Staff
body: We had a great stay here for six days while we were in London two weeks ago. We originally had a tiny room that was just not suitable for two people staying for almost a week. When we discussed it with the front desk they said they could change us the following day and they did, to a much bigger (but still small) room. Other than the extremely tiny first room our stay was very comfortable and the staff was very friendly and helpful. Two improvements we would suggest based on our stay: 1. Continental Breakfast Buffet - There really should be more to the menu's cooked food offerings than hardboiled eggs. A week of this unchanging and limited selection was a pretty underwhelming way to start our days. (We stayed in three other cities in the UK for the remainder of our two week holiday where the accommodations included the same 'continental breakfast buffet' we paid for at the Phoenix too, but unlike the Phoenix they had buffets that included bacon, sausage, scrambled eggs, fried eggs, beans, etc.). These foods are incidentally all available at the Phoenix, just at an extra charge. I am not sure if there was a surcharge for the buffet breakfast but knowing what I know now, I'd opt out of it. Really not worth paying for. 2. The Elevator - OUr first room (the closet sized one) was only a short walk up a single flight of stairs so we never used the lift at all. The reasonabley sized room however was on the third floor which after a day of sightseeing was not so easily accessed by weary feet. Stairs were also out of the quesgtion for luggage and laundry days too. The elevator however, is terrible. It is slow and small and people queue at every floor for it so even when it chooses to stop, it is loaded full of people and you have to wait some more. The lift needs to be more efficient to move people more quickly between floors, especially since it is so small. I would recomend this hotel if you are able to stay on a lower floor or can manage using the stairs all the time. If you can opt out of breakfast for a lower rate, definately do so and just pay for a hot breakfast there or anywhere else or....grab a McMuffin on the way to the tube (McDonald's is across the street from the Bayswater station)

title: Relation price-quality of the service provided not that fair. Good location.
body: The location is good, you can take bus 148 from Victoria Station to Queensway (20 minutes), in front of Hyde Park or the Circle Line from Victoria Station to Bayswater (potentially slightly more time). Walking distance to the hotel. Area with shops; food stores; pharmacy; post office, etc. Walking distance (35 minutes flat walking) to Oxford Street. Front rooms are facing the gardens. Quite area. 24 hours reception. Some of the food stores close at 12 am. Wifi speed good and strong. The individual rooms are really tiny. The toilet is too small and narrow, not suitable for overweight or big people. The bed is comfy. The decoration is old (chair very heavy to move and uncomfortable). Please consider providing harder pillows, at least as an option. I was given a room with two levels (with stairs), the desk was downstairs and the TV is facing the bed, how could you possible to watch TV? The windows are too high, you cannot see anything at all (my bedroom was facing the courtyard so not that nice). There is not socket beside the bed. The lamp beside the bed does provide a tiny light. You could not possible read. The wardrobe doors do not open (slide doors). It is so tiny that is impossible to hand anything properly. Not point to have it, to use it. Very noise breakfast room; with tiny space between tables. Not good to have a relax reading (newspaper) when eating breakfast. I saw a couple of guests with a significant overweight and they were asked to sit in one individual table just beside another one. They could barely move. Breakfast average, not warm food (not English breakfast). Breakfast staff not that friendly with poor English (most of the staff from East of Europe). You are not allowed to do your own toast, which it is fine, but there are not options rather than slides bread. I asked for normal bread and it seemed such a big deal. The reception staff may be different, the male was very nice, but some of the girls are not friendly or welcoming at all. It is a real shame because the overall lounge is very nice and relaxing area to read or to have a drink. The staff from the bar usually are checking their mobiles. I was waiting for a while (30 minutes) until somebody turned up, and then checked the mobile again. When I checked out I was not asked how was my stay; it is hard to get a good morning; afternoon or evening from the receptionist even if I say so first. I only got a smile when I was leaving after asking for the 147 bus location for Victoria Station, which it was wrong and I was advised it was the 148 route. The cleaning staff were uniform as well as the breakfast staff. I am not sure whey the staff in the reception do not have uniforms. It would be fair and at the same time smarter. The checking out is at 11 am, which is reasonable. The hotel has a storage place, but the staff does not put any label or nothing. Anyone could take any suitcase and they would not take responsibility. Toiletries provided, good quality (hand soap; gel and shampoo; shower cap; tissues, which it is grateful). Hair drier old, useless. One hand-tower only is provided, please consider providing two (one for the hair). Cleaness good, I found a hair and urine in the toilet though. Kettle not empty. Please ensure emptying the kettle at all times. Tea bags were opened (two of them). I booked the hotel because I got a deal. But, I have checked the usual rates and they are an average of £85.00 per person and night (including breakfast). The price is expensive for the type of accommodation and the quality of the service provided unless you get a deal. The hotel also advertised rooms with bathroom. I am not sure if some of the bedrooms may have a bath, but certainly not the individual ones, which have a very tiny shower.

title: A Phoenix That Failed to Rise
body: This was our second visit to London. We chose Phoenix because it's very close to the hotel where we stayed during our first trip. So we're already familiar with the surrounding neighborhood. Upon our check-in, we got assigned to a room in the basement even though no disclosure was provided during the booking at all. The room is small but reasonably clean (the Armoire baseboard is very dusty). It's about 12x10 sq ft (not including a post-stamp size bathroom). The breakfast room is also in the basement, just next door. I guess that's the only advantage. In our room strangely the bathroom floor is raised by about 2.5-3 inches. This can be a safety hazard by tripping people who do not pay special attention to it. For the interior noise insulation, I would give a grade of D. You can unmistakably tell when someone upstairs is taking shower because the water splashing sounds like water is leaking through the floor. The bathroom in our basement unit also has some plumbing issue: the drainage is very slow for both shower stall and basin. If you're taking shower just a little longer or turning up the valve a little bit for more water, you will end up standing in a pool of water. Literally you would become a classic statue in a mini-fountain. I suspect other basement units would suffer from the same issue as well. We stayed for two nights only. The first night was relatively quiet, with only some background white noise from outside. The second night was sleepless for the most part because there were about 15-20 school kids who checked in that day. Even their teacher complained about them making too much noise on the following morning during breakfast. The breakfast room was always bustling during our stay. The continental breakfast choices can not be rated as excellent, but definitely good enough. The hotel staff are polite. There is no safe in our room, but the hotel does have deposit boxes near the reception desk. It's small but sufficient for the storage of passport, credit cards and some cash, etc. Two keys are required to open one. We only wish the hotel management at Phoenix could have been more forthcoming to disclose up-front during the booking if a room is in the basement, so that a guest can make a better, informed decision. The hotel should also have been a little wiser in handling a large group of noisy guests so that the other people could have had a more enjoyable and peaceful stay.

title: Modern, but needs improvement
body: The hotel is modern but seems to be in the middle of renovation. The lobby and breakfast area look newly renovated, but the rooms look like they are in the works. It was inviting, and we stayed as part of a tourist agency deal. For the price we paid, it wasn't bad. But I definitely have to get used to what Europe defines as four-star. Europe definitely utilizes every inch of space so the rooms were quite small. Breakfast was good. Traditional European breakfast, and there were waiters to seat us. Would not go out of my way to book again, but it was centrally located and accommodated all needs.

title: Never ever going back!
body: I just spend one of the worst nights ever in this hotel! Luckily we had only booked for one night, but had we booked for more nights, we would have left after one night anyway. We got this very very tiny room on the first floor. We could not pass each other by the bed, so little room ad we to move around. The window was to the backyard but all we could see was a wall. That made the room even smaller. The floor was uneven, the room was too hot. The worst thing was the bed. It was hard as a rock, so was the pillows. We slept horrible and woke up many times during the night. Woke up with a terrible headache and sore in our backs and necks. Our heads felt foggy and I actually got sick because the headache was so bad. I have never experienced anything like that. I can't imagine that anyone would be okay with sleeping on a bed like that - or that nay hotel would be okay with having bed as such. The fire alarm in the ceiling blinked on and off during the night. Sometimes red, sometimes green, sometimes not at all. The hotel was clean though, but I will never come back again. The room was not nice to spend time in, not big enough, cramped, stuffy and with heavy air. You could maybe think that it would be okay just to sleep in, but not even a good nights sleep could we get. We could not wait to get out of there in the morning, skipped breakfast because we felt so horrible and just had to get out in the air and out of that tiny room.

title: Love the room but staffs seem a bit snobbish
body: Currently staying here as I'm writing this. Here on a business trip, attended the world travel market. Love the room. Simple and clean. Breakfast is good enough for us. Simple and healthy. However, the staff members need to be more polite with clients. You may see us as a pair of young asians but we are more than that. We own a travel agency in Malaysia and most of our clients are VIPs. (Just saying).. and we wouldnt be here in the first place if we cant afford this trip.. So, even if you keep your hotel rooms pretty and clean, but staff's attitude should be taken into consideration as well. Reception staffs are good all the way from checking in and when we call to request for something. They seemed happy to help. But... When you deliver whatever things a client request for, you dont just knock and shove that thing on their faces as soon as they open the door and turn around with that snobby face of yours and not replying when the client says thank you. And when a client enters the breakfast room, you dont stare at them as if they're some homeless people who somehow got lost there. Even if you dont feel like welcoming them, you guys could at least smile. I mean, you didnt seem to have any trouble wishing other clients good morning or hello upon entering the room. Not sure if its racism or something else but the management need to fix this. You'll never know who you might be dealing with. You have a good hotel so dont let your staff ruin your reputation.

title: It's mostly about the location
body: The Phoenix is a quaint older style hotel with most of the basic amenities. The staff were not rude, but could have been a little friendlier. The room was very basic, but well maintained and clean. Unfortunately (or fortunately) for us, we were in the middle of a heat wave. Air conditioning is generally not required over in the UK. All we had was a fan and could only open the window slightly, to allow some fresh air to come in. The breakfast was OK, but fairly basic. The location is great. We were close to Queensway and Bayswater roads, and only a 5 minute walk to Kensington Gardens. In summary, I guess you should should shop around before choosing this Hotel. We really didn't see anything locally, that we could compare it to, so this may be the standard for the area.

body: I can accept a tiny room, but this was ridiculous in size. It was incredibly hot, and they did have a somewhat working fan that I found the 2nd night in a cupboard that was difficult to get to because of the bed. The worst thing, though, was the noise from the street. I was on the 2nd floor in the front for two nights before I gave up. You could hear any and everything that occurred from trash pickup, towing, idling engines, people talking... I would have to put it at the bottom of hotels I have ever stayed at.

title: Small Room, Good Location, Quiet
body: We stayed in the Phoenix the first weekend of September. The staff at the front desk were friendly, although check in/out was the only time we spoke to them. I had booked a double room but was given a twin, we had been travelling for hours so I decided to say nothing as I was too exhausted to double check the booking and ask to be moved. The hotel, despite the amount of guest was silent and we slept well, although there is no air-conditioning we kept the window opened all night. The room was very small and so was the bathroom. Decor in the bedroom was quite dated also but it was clean and tidy. Location is fantastic, 2 minutes from Bayswater tube station and about 5 minutes from Kensingston Palace Gardens. Breakfast was OK, continental so various cereals, meats, cheeses and pastries available.

title: Lovely hotel near everything you need
body: Lovely hotel, small room, I've stayed in smaller, it was clean and had everything you need. It was however very warm in the room so if this is going to spoil your break don't book here. There is a fan you can use and the window does open. It's just around the corner from two underground stations, lots of bars, restaurants and shops from Tesco express to cheap souvenirs. The bus tours go from Bayswater Road as well. But if you Cross Bayswater Road you can walk through Kensington Park which is lovely, Diana's memorial is in the park and fabulous playground. if you turn left out of the park you will come to The Albert Memorial and The Royal Albert Hall. Walk a little further and you'll be on Knightsbridge. If you do decide to walk back remember the park gates are locked at 9pm. Breakfast was great, usual continental with eggs, ham, cheese, fruit etc. All in all a great hotel in a great location, with everything you want for a great trip to London right on the doorstep. We will be back.

title: You have to be quite thin.
body: We've stayed here several times on our trips to London. In the meanwhile, they've renovated the whole hotel, which turned out to be very nice, modern and chic. The location is great, close to Kensington Gardens and Notting Hill, with tube stations, pubs, restaurants and shopping nearby, so there's always something to do. The romms are TINY, especially the bathrooms. When you're a bit chubbier you would hardly be able to use the toilet. The shower is tricky, weird mechanism to change the temperature. Tiny sink, every time I washed my face I flooded the whole room. Tiny TV as well. Breakfast is okay, it's nothing special but I can't really complain. The staff in the breakfast room are friendly and keen on keeping everything tidy and clean. They've even got some gluten free and vegan stuff. The staff are from Poland, nearly all of them. As mentioned before, the breakfast staff were very nice. Some of the receptionists however were not very friendly. Not saying hello or goodbye or even smiling once. A four star rating is not justified. Three stars would do.

body: We truly enjoyed our stay here. The location is perfect for transport, restaurants and shopping. Portobello Road Markets are around a fifteen minute walk from the hotel. Plus for those into movies Notting Hill is also in the same area, the location for the movie 'Notting Hill' with Hugh Grant and Julia Roberts. Breakfast is Continental with plentiful choices. The reason for our rating was the cleanliness of the rooms and changing of linen. Overall, I recommend staying at the Phoenix Hotel.

body: I stayed at the Phoenix hotel for 4 nights and it was nothing special but I guess you get what you pay for. My room was small but most important clean and the bathroom was nice. The furniture in the room was worn down and the bed was hard as a brick. It would be nice if there was a little fridge, a safety box and a full body mirror in the room which is more or less basic even in cheaper hotels these days. Location is great not far from two underground stations, close to Notting Hill and Kensington Gardens.

title: Would not recommend teensy room and beds are all standard doubles (140cm)
body: Chose this hotel nased on photographs on the website, rooms looked reasonable, simple but ok. Price very good and breakfast included with good reviews and certificate of excellence - seemed nothing could go wrong. Pros: hotel is very clean, linens good, breakfast reasonably good selection, staff friendly Cons: the room looks nothing like the photo on the hotel website - you could not fit an armchair next to the ved without using a chainsaw first - we have a double standard size bed (140cm wide) which i would not offer my guests at home, its not comfortable for 2 people. The hotel website does not state that beds are doible standard and the booking portals just say double room. Next to the bed there is 60cm so you can get into bed.on the other side 20cm to the window. the room feels claustrophobic. Bathroom ok size. All in all the price seems low but when you compare to other places another 40 pounds will get you a better experience which for me is worth it. Sadly no twin available or we would have moved.

title: Basic
body: We stayed at this London hotel prior to our cruise with less than high expectations as the hotels in central London are very expensive (and this one was moderately priced by comparison). We took a quad room (with 4 single beds). Upon arrival, we received a polite reception and found out that to get to a lift, you first had to carry heavy luggage down one flight of stairs (odd). All rooms have traditional keys (we would find this out later on in other London hotel). Not a problem (but seems impractical from the hotel's point of view), but ok. The room itself is very small (and loft style, 2 beds in a tiny loft and 2 beds in the lower main room). They had 2 tvs (which actually worked out fairly well) but here was the first surprise.. no air conditioning. London is VERY humid and the AC would have been convenient only to dry out the humid room. We had a fan in the room (and had to request another one for the upper part of the room). Thankfully, the hotel had plenty of fans and this helped us for sleeping. The beds themselves were comfortable however. Nice and plush but had heavy duvets (we had to request sheets in order to sleep more comfortably). Bathroom... clean but again small. More practical than luxurious. No room for toileteries. Odd that they would keep bathrooms minimalist but have tons of furniture in the rest of the room that did not seem to have a purpose (nor look like it belonged there). On that note, the hotel should really get rid of this useless furniture to make more room to actually walk around. No ice machines, no vending machines (nor here or in most hotels in London). Seriously? To my fell North American readers... Do not expect the same level of service as we get in Canada and US. You will not get it (even for the high prices that they charge). This was our experience here (and other hotel that we stayed at in London). The breakfast that was included was ok. Not huge variety of fruit (actually, almost none). Again, basic but not too bad (we all ate well). There are nearby restaurants with great big breakfast offerings for not too expensive. Customer service at hotel was also... basic. Not overly friendly but not rude (except at breakfast, rushed and unfriendly). We are used to being asked HOW WAS YOUR STAY. You won't get that level of care here. It is a basic question and shows that the staff care about your experience in their hotel. I would recommend if only that this could be as good as it gets for the location at this price.

title: Brilliant Location, Disappointing Single Room
body: Single room was a disappointment to be honest. From the pictures on the website, and other reviews, I expected slightly more. Very small, scruffy furniture (desk and wardrobe) and marks on the wall. Bathroom was extremely clean. Other areas of the hotel look gorgeous. Just a shame that single rooms are on the noisy front end of the hotel, like an add on. However, I was here on business and was only in the room for 8 hours sleeping- the location was excellent for the tube (Bayswater).

title: Would not recommend
body: Our room was little more than a shoebox. The room had a freestanding closet, a double bed, a desk and chair, and a table in a room that was barely big enough for the bed. The door wouldn't open all the way because the closet was in the way. The bathroom was so tiny that we couldn't even get dressed in it after a shower. The shower itself was so small that my elbows smacked into the sides of it every time I moved. On the plus side, it was clean, most of the staff were helpful, and it has a good location.

title: Excellent location and good hotel
body: The best asset for the hotel is it's location, about 5 minutes walk from two tube stations, Bayswater (circle and district) and Queensway (Central) which cover the vast majority of all attractions. It's only 7-8 minutes walk from Hyde Park, 12-15 minutes from Kensington Palace. The room we had was clean and functional, although quite basic compared to the fancy lobby. We had two singles beds which was ok, we had booked a twin room. Breakfast was continental and again good. The only concern was collecting the key at reception. The key was left in at reception each time we left the hotel and collected upon return, but there didn't seem to be any questions when we asked for the key. The hotel then said they were not liable for any thefts from the room. I'm not sure how this could be to be honest. I would recommend this hotel, with the only caveat being the way the room key is handled. The area has a lot of shops and restaurants.

title: Great short stay
body: Had to make a quick visit to London for a few days and after doing an extensive search for the best hotel in the best location for the best price in one of the most busy and expensive cities in the world - Phoenix got my pick and no regrets. Apart from the really squeaky floors (stay away from rooms 314-318, the floors above are loud when walked on) and thin walls, it was a good stay for what I needed. Very conveniently located near Whiteleys (small mall) and other stores which you may need during your stay (incl Boots Pharmacy which opens til midnight weeknights!). Don't expect flashy rooms! It's very simple and I'm glad I didn't have to spend that much time in the hotel.

title: Comfy but staff could be nicer
body: Stayed here for 3 weeks in February 2016. We booked the night before our arrival, so we could book straight in after arriving on a very early flight, emails were sent stating this, emails back comfiming that our room will be ready for our early arrival. Upon arrival we were met with a very rude "you were meant to be here yesterday" the rudeness continued for the next 3 weeks. Always said good morning, good afternoon, hello and good bye to staff and only ONE staff member engaged in chat with us. Room was comfy, small but comfy, very warm and couldn't turn the heating down, so had to use a small fan to cool the room down. The bathroom had no exhaust fans, so after showering you had to open the bathroom door, to get fresh air in and let the steam out from your shower. Internet worked great for our stay, renovations going on on our floor that we were not informed about. Free breakfast was a great way to start the day, just don't ask the rude staff to heat up anything for you.... Would stay here again based ONLY on location, so close to Paddington, Bayswater and Queensway stations. So close to Kensington Palace and other touristy places of interest. BUT Based in friendliness of staff...NOPE would not recommend. Lots of great place to get a bite to eat and lovely parks near by to wander through and loads of squirrels and birds to feed.

body: Location is great and most areas are clean. Wifi can be pretty hopeless. You can wait ages for a slow lift. Quite noisy and poorly insulated for noise. Breakfast below par. title: Good location, buy noisy and dated
body: Reading other reviews, I can only assume that some rooms are *much* better than others... and I must've got a dud. Good points: - Reception was well-presented. - Wifi was free. - Only a short walk to the station and shops. - It seemed clean. Bad points: - Check-in was painful and they couldn't find my booking, initially suggesting I'd maybe booked the hotel next door! - The room was very dated (I'm guessing 1980's), drab and tatty. A wardrobe with no doors squeezed in at the end of the tiny bed. TV mounted next to the bed and high up - making it very difficult to watch. - Very compact bathroom with a shower door that needed brute force to move. I'm not sure how a larger person would've coped. - No soundproofing either internally (I could hear everything from both rooms next door) or externally (I could hear conversations on the street so clearly I initially thought the window was open). This really wasn't helped that the room doors were seriously over-sprung and crashed shut every time anyone left their room. - No ventilation, and it was really hot even in Winter. - Very poor security: It's archaic handing back in keys, but no ID checks is astonishing... I just said my room number and got given the key without hesitation! - The cleaners began rattling doors at 8AM and repeated every 15 minutes until I left! I've stayed in lots of London hotels and I have no issues whatsoever with the small room size. But easy check-in, low noise and ventilation are vital. This place failed on all. I'd love to support smaller hotels, but this was really disappointing in light of so many positive reviews.

title: Marvellous location in Central London, great pricing though tiny rooms!
body: Difficult to find as centrally located a place in Bayswater/Queensway area in London. Nice buffet breakfast though very business like and one has tens of restaurants and eateries just a few minutes of walk from here. Great Persian, Indian and Lebanese food in the vicinity. Being located bang opposite Whiteleys shopping mall added advantage. At the other end of Hyde park is also not a bad option. Not very pleased with the tiny and noisy lift though! But recommended for business travellers as well as holidaying.

title: Cosy but a little too warm
body: Decent hotel, the staff were friendly, breakfast was nice; however, our room was extremely hot. We opened the window and had the fan on but it still wasn't cool enough to get a full nights sleep. Also, the beds were very hard, which didn't help either. The bathroom was nice, did the job and the shower was great (although my 6 foot partner couldn't fit under the shower head!) Great location, shops out on the main street but the hotel itself was tucked away a bit so it wasn't too loud. Plenty of places to eat for lunch and dinner. We had the continental breakfast; basic, but again, did the job.

title: Decent hotel to pop into for a quick stay in London
body: We stayed at the Phoenix for three nights. I loved the view from our window, which looked out onto a park. The room was quite spacious I think. Even once we had plopped our quite large travel cases on the floor, we still had plenty of room to move about. The heating was a bit stifling with any kind of long apparel being worn, but we could open our windows enough to let fresh air in. The front desk staff were polite. The English lady in the breakfast room was bubbly and helpful. The continental buffet is the same selection of products every morning so did become quite mundane, and we sort of felt like we had to rush through our food to make space for other guests. Sort of like a production line of people. Overall, we had a pleasant enough stay with somewhere comfortable to put our heads for the night.

title: Decent for the price
body: With the expensive city of London, this place was OK. The room was not large, but fit two people ok. Bed was comfy, and added tea, coffee, and bath supplies was fine. No pictures in the room, plain, but functional. Windows opened easily, due to the high heat in the place. We turned off the heater, but still it was warm. With the windows open, the vehicles and people walking about were very noticeable. Bring earplugs for sound sleeping, which I use most places anyway. Bath facilities were fine and the Breakfast was ok with boiled eggs, pastries, meat and cheeses, toast, bagels, 3 juices, and many different kinds of cereals. Front desk was nice and helpful, but food servers were not cheerful in the morning, but they were helpful. Free wifi, but it was slow at times.

body: The hotel is very clean and well maintained and very accessible from the Queensway and Bayswater tube stations - Oxford circus is just 2 stops away. If you are looking for a convenience of staying and moving around in London and this is really good place with respect to cleanliness and transport access.The quaint multi ethnic shops nearby offer a good and pleasant stroll in the evenings. The other side below... You can bite into a piece of history of sorts while selecting to stay at the the Phoenix London - creaky elevator which makes you want to count the creaks as it closes and opens. And you can hear your neighbor above walking footsteps at times and there is no light displaying the hotel name. Good possibility you could forget the way back if you stroll out. The room was pretty too small. If i had a few more beers, the bath area was too small to stand and take a bath.I'm thin luckily. Continental breakfast is the same fare daily - not impressive.

title: Mostly okay
body: The Phoenix is a typical London hotel and quite acceptable value for money. The location is excellent - close to Hyde Park, and in easy walking distance of both Bayswater and Queensway tube stations. The hotel is in a quiet side street with little or no street noise. The rooms and common areas are a little dark and tired looking, but everything works. There is only one lift which is small and quite slow, so around breakfast and check-out time you should expect queues on almost every floor. The staff is polite but not exactly friendly. Before arriving at The Phoenix, I was staying in a countryside hotel. The difference in service level was huge! Breakfast selection is not very interesting, and the breakfast room is cramped and busy. WiFi was slow and unstable. I wouldn't recommend The Phoenix for a romantic getaway, but for a business trip or similar, it serves its purpose.

title: Well located but rooms leave a lot to be desired!
body: I shared a twin bed room at the Phoenix with my daughter, for a weekend in February 2015. The hotel is well located and the common areas are decent enough but the room itself was pokey at very best and the beds very narrow and drab looking. The bathroom definitely not big enough for two to brush their teeth at the same time, the carpets tacky, no safe, the cupboard unable to close or open without much noise and force. We were only there for a weekend and out all day but it really was rather disappointing!

body: The room was probably the smallest i've ever stayed in (especially the bathroom... You may have to suck your gut in to get past the sink to the toilet) but it was clean and worked fine as a decent and affordable place to crash during my London trip. Staff was courteous and helpful so no complaints there. I would recommend this to anyone looking for an affordable place to stay while in London.

title: Great location, fine service but an old building
body: I don't consider this hotel to be mediocre, by no means. The staff is friendly and the front ofice people helped us out in a fine way when we were not completely satisfied with our first room. We instantly got another room without discussion! :-) The breakfast is also ok. Not great, but enough choice for every taste. The English breakfast (additional fee) is great, but one needs to have some patience. The difference between 3 and 4 stars is the hotel building. This is just not what you expect from a modern hotel building. The building is a bit outdated. Not a bit fancy or anything else fancy. A bit old. The safety deposit boxes are at the front desk while most modern hotels have inroom safety deposit boxes. Small breakfast room. The location of the hotel is great: close to 2 underground stations and the many many restaurants and shops of Queensway.

body: This isn't the fanciest of hotels but it certainly did the trick for us in London. The proximity of its location to two subway stations was the biggest plus. title: Great location in central London
body: I stayed at the Phoenix Hotel for 12 nights in a 1 bedroom. Location is fantastic. Less than a 5 minute walk from Bayswater Tube station (Circle and District line) and a 7 minute further walk to Queensway (Central line). Plenty of shops and restaurants including a small shopping centre all close by Reception were very helpful and friendly. Helped me arrange a taxi with no issues. The bedroom itself was clean but a little small. This was the only small issue. The bathroom was tiny. The basin was very small. The hotel does not have air conditioning but a fan was provided. The room had excellent free wifi Included breakfast was very good also. A good variety of options. Did not leave feeling still hungry A great hotel with a fantastic location. If you dont mind a small bathroom then I would recommend this place. I would stay here again

title: Very Small single room
body: Had 1 night at this hotel recently. It was reasonable for central London being £59 per night over easter. The only gripe being the room was quite small and the bed small as in a single which I knew anyway. The bathroom was tiny. Had one of those silly basins when you washed your face you nearly cracked your nose on this stupid shelf directly above it. Why do hotels do this? You got a continental breakfast in with the price so altogether not a bad deal and in fairness I would stay at the hotel again, however I would opt for a twin room if I was going to stay longer as I think more than one night in this room would be too much for me especially In the summer when it is hot and humid the room must be unbearable. Very central location being near Queensway Tube and Bayswater tube and Whiteleys shopping centre around the corner. 10mins slow walk to Hyde Park. I must say very clean. Couldn't fault that at all. I would recommend this hotel but again you only get what you pay for so for the price don't expect the Ritz but a very fair deal.

title: Four stars for value for London, three stars for comfort
body: Firstly, this hotel is excellent value for a hotel in London - that is really important to state. The location is also very convenient. I think I've learnt my lesson, though, to book a double room if I am traveling solo, as I found the little single room a bit depressing! It was more than adequate though, and the bed was comfy. The rooms have a TV and a good shower room. As I was on my own, the breakfast staff put me on a table which had been only separated minimally from the couple next to me, which made me feel a bit awkward (and another day I had a man coughing and spluttering over me). The breakfast room in general was busy and claustrophobic, but for the price you would not usually expect a breakfast, so I just downed my croissant and ran! In summary: excellent value, and just what you'd expect for the money - clean, comfortable but nothing special.

title: Basic Hotel, good location
body: The location is a selling point, being only a 2 minute walk from Bayswater tube station yet situated on a quiet street. The staff were friendly and I overheard them converse in several languages with guests. The room however was shoebox size, had basic toiletries but quite a decent bathroom. The elevator was always busy which sometimes meant a long wait. Being on the 3rd floor, I was often able to get to our room quicker using the stairs. Breakfast was a reasonable continental, although did lack variety. Cooked breakfast available at extra cost on request. There was a small bar/lounge and a nice open reception area. Slightly overpriced overall, but it is London.

body: This is a lovely looking hotel and the immediate area is quiet so no noise from outside which can often be a problem in London. The trouble we has was the noise from internal doors as there are no sliders so they bang. We were woken at 2am by people coming in and then from 7am from people leaving so not the greatest sleep. The rooms are very small and hot and though the staff are helpful they do not speak great english which was apparent more so at breakfast. We got coffee instead of tea and 3 out of 4 of us did not receive the food we ordered. The bar and lobby areas are comfortable and the gent behind the bar was very friendly.

title: Downgrading My Score from 4 to (barely) 3 Stars
body: So, I've stayed in this hotel on a few occasions since 2006. As a rule, it's been pretty great. The common areas have gotten a bit of a face lift in the past year or so, and generally speaking, it seems the rooms in general are holding up okay. But the beds leave a good bit to be desired these days, at least in room 202. It's a spring type mattress, which is fine in theory, but there's precious little padding between those painful bits of steel and my ribs. Frankly, it's an *extremely* cheap mattress, and this is just not the place where a hotel should cut corners. It's just unacceptable. This is not the kind of hotel you spend time in. It's supposed to be a cozy place to sleep, shower, have your breakfast, and little more. If you can't sleep because the bedding is just that awful, there's not much point, is there? If you're on a tighter, it still may be a better alternative than the expensive chains (e.g. Hilton and their brethren) and posh boutique hotels. It's also better than some of the sad excuses for accommodations you'll find at some cut-rate operations But you'll be getting what you pay for, and that may include a sleepless night or two. To this hotel's General Manager and ownership, I say this: You can do better.

title: Great location, lacking in service
body: I stayed here on business on 25th September, I booked a double room, and was given a twin. The public areas of the hotel are clean and well appointed, but the rooms are well overdue an upgrade. They we're clean though. Though breakfast was paid for, when I went to breakfast, there were no available seats, and unlike other hotels, there were no staff helping guests to tables.....so I stood in the breakfast room and helped myself to a juice and toast. Before checking out, I waited in the lobby for my colleague, and felt very much in the way as the house keeping staff were cleaning around me.....despite the bar and lounge being empty. So whilst I didn't have an unpleasant stay, it was certainly not a great one, and would only really stay here again if it were necessary for work.

title: Great location and good for the money
body: This hotel suited my needs well as I could walk to many restaurants down the street and two tube stops were a five minute walk around the block. Staff was friendly and breakfast setup was great. I ate breakfast with a family from New Zealand one morning. Room was small but big enough for what I was needing. A clean place to stay with a bathroom and bed and a tv. The only thing when I was there, was that there was construction going on so it was a bit loud and I was not used to no air con so I kept my window open a lot. You can also hear everything in the hall including the elevator. I'd recommend staying further down the hall if you can. This is for people on a budget like me and looking not to stay in a hostel but do not need luxury.

title: Great location, small room
body: My husband and I stayed at this hotel for three nights and were provided with a very small room in what seem to be lower ground floor under street level, with a window looking out to a small enclosed courtyard. With no air conditioning, a very small desk fan and no ability for a breeze to come in the window, we found the room uncomfortable to sleep in. It had a double bed, two small bedside tables, small wardrobe and a desk with mirror with no room to open a suitcase. One suitcase was partially stored in the wardrobe and the other at the end of the bed therefore only able to access the bed from the base of the bed, no room to walk around. Shower en-suite and separate toilet had been recently renovated and were very clean and tidy however as the room was so small the shower room had no door therefore no privacy from the bedroom when having a shower. On a positive note, reception staff very friendly, the breakfast was fresh and adequate and the location fantastic. Easy walking distance to Hyde Park and the tube, even with luggage.

title: Oh Dear
body: This is awful. Where to start? Very small room. Spoke to reception about organising an early breakfast as we had a tour to meet. They were fine with this and one of the young men from reception actually brought us our coffee in the dining room from the kitchen. There was also another couple having an early breakfast. I poked my head in to the kitchen as the receptionist had gone and asked the woman there for another coffee. Wow, did I get into trouble. Obviously no one had told her there would be people in early for breakfast and she was really angry and told me to get out until 7 am. I didn't say anything at the time as she may not have been feeling well. After we had left the hotel to join another tour I realised my camera was missing. It had been sitting beside my suitcase in the hotel room. I called the Phoenix and they said they would check with housekeeping. No one bothered to ring back. Not somewhere I would recommend staying.

title: Not Magic.
body: Harry Potter and the Phoenix Hotel. I was surprised to be put in Harry's room under the stairs - a tiny airless room. Still I thought, there will be a nice shower, but the optical illusion trick of the step meant a sharp step down jarring my leg. Well, I can rest it on the bed. No, wait, the uncomfortable hard bed? Clearly not. Watch some TV, take my mind off it?- The TV on the wall nailed at an angle that means I cannot see from the bed very well -that TV? So that's a no then. I'll phone home- have a chat. Sorry, no air waves here - you have to suffer in silence. Sleep then. Yes, for two hours, then hear all the merry folk next door arriving, shouting, shutting anything they can find. What fun. Dawn in London - perhaps I will hear the nightingale sing in Kensington Gardens Square- after all I walked for 3/4 of an hour to find it after the Florist near Bayswater Tube station-clearly in disguise as a death eater- sent me completely the wrong way. The walls start to move in even further and claustrophobia starts to grip. I pack, and go down for breakfast - oh it's another stuffy room, where the windows appear to have actually been glued shut in case of invasion, and I am treated to cheek by jowl stories of London by cheerful American visitors 6 inches away from my arm, while unsmiling waitresses talk loudly in a foreign language across the room pretending I do not exist. The cheese and ham glares at me. (Who is it that eats cheese and ham for Breakfast?) The Toast is made of a substance I do not recognise. It has not been magic. I leave and and go and sit in a cafe where I can have a hot drink (not from a lukewarm thermos flask) and smell the air- rather than my fellow diner. Reflecting on my story I would say The Phoenix Hotel, which does not serve Dinner or cook breakfast, is in disguise as a Bed and Breakfast in a cupboard, with no frills, ambiance or atmosphere but London costs, so if this is what you are after, then you are in for a treat, but if not, you have been warned in this tale of Harry Potter's bedroom at the Phoenix Hotel, Bayswater.

title: Look around for something else
body: My stay wasn't all negative, the hotel is close to transport, and lots of great restaurants, but while I was there the hotel was undergoing major renovations, and there was constant dodging of workmen, but I can overlook that. My room was small, and constantly smelled of cigarette smoke to the point my towels even smelled like smoke, something I find totally unacceptable. The room had squeaky floorboards and every time someone in the next room trod on them, it squeaked in my room. My room neighbours were extremely noisy, and slammed doors all night, I did complain, but this only led to more door slamming, and banging on my door in the wee hours. I was on the first floor, and the truck to collect dirty linen arrive between 10pm & 2am, and would be right under my window and wake me every night. To top it off, when my driver collected me as I was leaving, the owner of the hotel abused him because he was carrying a coffee. Very disappointing.

title: Never again!
body: I thought the hotel was very bad. The reception was undergoing a major renovation, it looks awful! I wasn't informed of that before my stay! It just looks like a cheap hostel rather than a hotel. The location is great and building looks good from the outside...so what! Inside it's very mediocre place. The corridors are so narrow I couldn't fit in with my luggage! The room is outdated with nasty bits on the wall, bed uncomfortable, furniture old. The bathroom was quite new but..the major issue was...there was a VERY BAD smell in the room! It was kind of like someone was smoking in the room and tried to cover it with some perfume..I found out later it could have been chemicals sprayed over the room...it gave me a massive headache and I have had the window open all night not to feel dizzy in this terrible smell! I mean, really...when I got to the hotel I was thinking why I was so stupid to book such a terrible place...£53 a night in such a good location in London...there must have been something wrong about it...and I stayed at 3* Best Western before and they weren't event close as bad as this place. A disgraceful 1* hostel that;s what it is. I just went to sleep immediately and wanted to get out of there in the morning as soon as possible! Don't waste you time, health and money to stay there! NEVER AGAIN!!!!!!!!!!!!! This is the worst hotel I ever stayed at!

It was kind of like someone was smoking in the room and tried to cover it with some perfume..I found out later it could have been chemicals sprayed over the room...it gave me a massive headache and I have had the window open all night not to feel dizzy in this terrible smell! I mean, really...when I got to the hotel I was thinking why I was so stupid to book such a terrible place...£53 a night in such a good location in London...there must have been something wrong about it...and I stayed at 3* Best Western before and they weren't event close as bad as this place. A disgraceful 1* hostel that;s what it is. I just went to sleep immediately and wanted to get out of there in the morning as soon as possible! Don't waste you time, health and money to stay there! NEVER AGAIN!!!!!!!!!!!!! This is the worst hotel I ever stayed at!
