title: Good location, price but a little down at the heels
body: This is my third stay at this property. I stayed at this hotel on two previous trips... four years ago and two years ago. Unfortunately I discovered that the overall appearance of the hotel has deteriorated since my last visit. The hotel has become somewhat shabby .... carpets, furniture, walls etc. all show signs of wear and tear. I would hope that a reno is planned for the near future. There is nothing glaringly wrong with the hotel... it is just "tired". I was given a room facing the street and positioned right above the entrance facade. There is no AC. London was in the middle of a heat wave and my room was like an oven all night and all day. I had the window open but it did not allow much air circulation. Then, due to the window being opened, I had to deal with street noise of people walking by talking, cars, glass bottles being regularly dumped into a dumpster... On the day I checked in, there were several people at reception very unhappy with the warmth of the rooms. One couple were checking out and moving somewhere else as the hotel could not even provide a fan for them. Another group were very angry and upset. The staff attempted to explain that such heat waves are rare in London and that many hotels are not prepared for such weather. My room was very small .... single bed pushed against a wall. The bed was reasonably comfortable. Pillows were hard. Duvet was a very heavy covering.. suitable for winter stays but not for summer. The breakfast room is downstairs.... if you arrived before 830, it was not too busy. But after that time..... really crowded and busy. I have returned to this hotel now 3 times due primarily to its location. It is a short 10 min. walk to Kensington Park, 5 min. walk to the underground stop Bayswater. The nearby streets have lots of little restaurants, souvenir shops, a grocery store, a pharmacy... all only a 2 min. or so walk away. Since my last stay, I found that the staff, both at the reception and in the breakfast room, have been replaced by workers from other EU countries where English is not the first language spoken. I found that my conversations with the employees at times was hampered by their lack of English or I found it difficult to understand their accented pronunciations. The reception staff were helpful whereas the breakfast staff seemed very shy and reserved. Would I stay here again? Perhaps, but not in the summer as it is too busy, and potentially too hot( My previous stays were in March and September) More likely, I will look at other properties in the area for my next trip to London.

title: would not stay again.
body: Great location, lots of restaurants/pubs and shops near by, tube station about a minute walk away (bayswater) and the staff were all very lovely- thats the good points. Unfortunately i wouldn't stay again, the room was extremely small. by far the smallest hotel room iv ever stayed in, london is very hectic and it would of been nice to have somewhere to sit and relax for an hour or so before heading out in the evening, but it just wasnt possible in that room, it was also extremely hot, we opened the window as much as we could, we were given a small fan but there were no plug sockets near the bed so we had to plug it in by the window so you couldn't feel it when you were trying to sleep at all. Decor was very dated, carpet looked very dirty i would recommend slippers or enough socks, bed was clean as was the bathroom, only 1 light in the room worked, all others were broken, I think maybe if you ask for a twin room instead of a double the room may be a little bit bigger as there was no way they could get 2 single beds with a gap between them in our room. very uncomfortable stay with lack of room and heat. Breakfast was ok, not alot of choice. i would definitely stay in this area again but not this hotel.

title: Nice hotel close to the metro.
body: This BW is situated in a reasonably nice area, close to metro stop. There was wifi access in the room. What they don't tell you is the lobby is not located on street level. You must lug your baggage up several steps. No porter to help. If that's not enough hassle, some rooms are not accessible by elevator. Once again, you must carry baggage a flight of stairs. The room, which I booked as a double for single person, was small, with no air conditioning. My one big piece of luggage could not remain on the floor if I was moving around the room. The bathroom was reasonable in size. My window which must remain open for circulation. The weather in London this day was warm. If you are booking this hotel, confirm room accessibility before booking.

title: Not the greatest...
body: We spent 6 nights here and wouldn't do it again...certainly would have considered a move if we hadn't prepaid. The room was small, the bed was hard and uncomfortable with inly one type of bedding available. There was NO air-conditioning which made it very uncomfortable at night in the hot temps that we had. We couldn't leave the windows open at night due to the street noise. (if you do stay here ask for a room that doesn't have street frontage I think the rooms on the other side might be a little more quiet). The bathroom was small with very little room to move. The breakfast room was busy, the food basic but OK, the breakfast staff were amazing at keeping things in order. Reception was not that welcoming with VERY wilted flower arrangements that were there from the time we arrived till we left. Better to have none that wilted dried up arrangements. We felt this place was more like a glorified Bed and Breakfast. No room service available for meals and while it says there is a restaurant it turned out to be the breakfast room and the bar wasn't much to write home about and it only served sandwiches. But there were a number of restaurants nearby withing 5 minutes walking distance. It was handy to train stations but was a fair stride to tourist attractions.

title: A place to sleep but nothing great
body: We spent 8 nights in this hotel. We might have changed in other circumstances but we had prepaid and got a fair deal. The price was expensive compared to other European hotels but OK for London. The hotel looks great from the outside and the reception service is good. The room itself was a bit small but the bathroom was tiny and hot. We had two single beds instead of a double and we were not able to change it because of the design of the room. There was no air conditioning. This is a problem, we found out, if the temp outside is above 23c. The walls are thin and we were able to hear our neighbours more than we would have liked. The breakfast room was overcrowded although the staff did their best to make it work. The choice of food was limited but good enough to fill your stomach. However, after the 6th morning of the same thing, we decided to go out and pay for breakfast. This wasn't necessarily a simple thing because the local cafés were dodgy. If we go to London again we will only stay in an apartment even though it will cost more.

title: Noisy but convenient location. Comfortable stay.
body: Stayed for 7 nights. Small but comfortable room with twin beds. Tea and instant coffee provided with tea kettle, but no coffee maker. Our room did not have a clock radio or an iron. We requested an iron from front desk and received it right away. There are no plug-ins in the bathroom but adequate plug ins in the main room. The staff were friendly and helpful, particularly the girls working in the breakfast room. Breakfast was good variety and filling. Location was great but noisy at night. Lots of different restaurants in the area and a shopping centre and pharmacy just down the street as well as 2 tube stations (Bayswater and Queensway). If you are interested in a bus tour, front desk can arrange it for you and the pickup point is about a 10 minute walk away in front of a Shell gas station. There is no ice machine, but ice can be requested from front desk or bar. Someone is at the desk 24 hours and you have to buzz each time you want to be let in. There is only one elevator and it is very slow.

title: Good location to Hyde Park, but...
body: The hotel is only a few blocks from Hyde Park and close to the Bayswater Tube station. The neighborhood is not that great. The restaurants near the hotel are so-so (don't eat at the Pub at the southeat corner of Queensway and Porchester Gardens). The Hop-on Hop-off bus has a stop on Bayswater Rd east of Queensway. The hotel staff were not from the UK and did not speak very good English (our hotel staff in Paris spoke better English). The staff was there to "take care of business", but beyond that they did not go out of their way to take any interest in you or your trip. The hotel has a free breakfast and it's very good. So overall it's close to the Tube, Hyde Park and the Hop-on bus, and the Hotel price is a good value with breakfast included; but the neighborhood and nearby restaurants are not that good, and the staff is not that great.

title: A place to stay
body: EK Airbus A380-800 flight to London was excellent, chauffeur drive super, without complimentary chauffeur drive we probably wouldn't be able to find the hotel. Actually it is close to the subway station, better get a weekly-card (Oyster Card). The hotel looks much better on the photo than it is, but it is a nice place "to stay". The receptionists from Polandand France have been very polite, but a little bit more action and smiling would be appreciated. Our room was clean, organized, not that big though. It is more like you stepping on someone's feet if there are two of you living together. The hotel is well located, the breakfast: not many options except, bread, ham, toast, cheese, butter, some fruits, but if you want to go for vegetables: eat the decoration like I did. If you are early enough you might get some tomatoes from the decoration, sometimes some slices of cucumber. If you would like to have another choice, order your ham and eggs / baked beans with sausages are also available upon request. (not complimentary).

title: Don't listen to the whiners
body: After reading some of the reviews I can't believe what stresses people out " if the speed of a lift is all you have to worry about, your a very lucky person", don't listen to people who whine look at the facts of all the reviews. This is a 3 star hotel not the Ritz so don't be booking this if you want the luxuries of a 5 star hotel. We stay in 5 star hotels all over the world but we decided to try this out as we got a very good deal. The hotel is 5 mins from Bayswater Tube station which is ideal and 8 mins walk from open topped tourist buses. I have never seen so many varied restaurants in one area and we ate, Mexican, Lebanese, Italian and Chinese for our evening meal the nights we were there and all good except the Chinese in the Whitely's mall at the end of the street, wish we had chosen one of the better ones on the Queensways only 5 mins away. The hotel was clean with an abundance of toiletries in bathroom, plenty of tea and coffee with two packs of biscuits and two sachets of galaxy hot chocolate. The continental breakfast was as you expect, croissants, cereal, toast and preserves, boiled eggs, muffins, orange juice etc you can upgrade to full English for £7.50. In hindsight I would of asked for room only and bought Cooked English breakfast as continental was £6. We had a quad room which was spacious but I heard some twins were quite small. The staff were friendly and helpful, if you had a bit conversation with them they get to know you and have your key immediately on arrival and are much more obliging. There was a small bar £3.60 for a pint of lager which I didn't feel to bad. Only negative was no aircon like usual 5 star but they provide a fan in your wardrobe, but not many people in the uk have air on in there bedrooms at home so do what you would do in uk, open a window, throw off the quilt and I am sure you'll manage. It was 25 degrees on some days which were a bit warm at night but not the end of the world and it didn't rain. Hotel was decent 3 star and exceeded our expectations of the star rating as we had nearly everything we needed and good location for transport links to the centre.

body: Booked four nights. The hotel is about five blocks from the train station, but took a while to find as it's down a side street. Front desk crowded and service very slow. Elevator seems to be run by gerbil power (and big enough to just hold two cuddling gerbils): slowest elevator I found in London! Walked up the stairs most of the time. Room was tiny, with small shower. Bed not great, but acceptable (although small). Bar was merely OK. Better places around the hotel for drinks and food. Not a place I will return to as the value and service just were not there.

title: Maybe not in the summer!
body: Another nice stay at the Phoenix Hotel. The problem with a summer stay is that there is no air-conditioning and the rooms get very hot. The hotel is fine at other times of the year - it is very convenient for Bayswater and Queensway tube stations and for a walk in Kensington Gardens. Just down the street is the Café Anglais for a chic setting and an excellent meal (either snack - soup/omelette or full-course delicious dinner). Next door on the corner is Whiteley's department store which has lots of different shops to explore! Have a good time!

title: Good choice for a short break
body: Let me start by saying there is nothing wrong with this hotel and if you need somewhere reasonably priced in London to stay for a couple of nights then this is somewhere you should consider. If there was a three-and-a-half rating on TripAdvisor that's what I'd give it. It is a couple of minutes from Queensway tube station, a 15-minute walk from Paddington station and situated just north of Kensington Gardens. Plenty of shops, cafes and bars close by. Breakfast is OK, but nothing to rave about. No room service other than snacks. My room was a decent size, clean and comfortable. So, if you need a base to explore London and are not too bothered about staying somewhere grand or modern this could be an option for you.

title: Great Location but no air conditioning!!!
body: This hotel is in a great area and is a short stroll to 2 tube stations, Bayswater and Queensway and it is a couple of stops to Paddngton Station. It is a block from Hyde Park and has a vibrant high street with great restaurants, shopping that are open fairly late. It is a safe neighborhood for walking later at night also. Our family loves boutique style hotels but no air conditioning during the recent heat wave in London really hampered our enjoyment of our short stay there. We stayed in the family room with 4 beds and it was bright and fairly spacious for Europe standards but it was up to 29 degrees Celsius some evenings and the fans provided didn't help much. Some great staff there, Tolis and Voila especially but some of the front reception staff were not helpful and welcoming. We understand London was busy for the Olympics but we didn't get a good impression from the front lines staff when we checked in. Decent breakfast in the morning, okay bar. It was great to have free wi-fi and be able to print off boarding passes etc. at the computer for all the guests. One thing we realized about London is that with the excellent transportation system you can stay almost anywhere but get air conditioning in the summer!!!

The location is great close to the tube with pubs, restaurants & shops close by but far enough off the High St that there is hardly any noise. The breakfast was average no better or worse than many other hotels i've stayed at and the staff were pleasant and helpful enough although I think they must be all trainees as they were all very young and of many nationalities.

The experience didn’t improve, being left to find my own way to the room, no direction offered by the staff, who where much more interested in chattering then dealing with a paying customer. The room was more tiered then me, old tatty, grubby, neglected, small, run down, noisy, the list is endless. Just to say you have to sit at an angle with the bathroom door open to use the toilet, that’s how small it is… Breakfast, it a joke guests lining up in a the underground dungeon waiting for a table, this was the end for me, time to check out.

title: Pleasant, comfortable, but...
body: A pleasant, comfortable hotel. Our twin bedroom was a decent size by townhouse conversion standards, but the toilet/shower room was very small with a tricky little step into it. The room was single glazed. There was a very good selection for Continental breakfast. However the quality of the bakery goods was indifferent with particularly chewy rolls. The breakfast staff was pleasant and attentive. it was a bit off putting to see an insect crawling across an adjoining table cloth. The bar has a very limited selection. Some of the furnishings in the public areas is in need of attention[e.g. the carpet by lift doors]. The cleanliness is very high throughout. There is a complimentary luggage room. It's position is in a quiet street off cosmopolitain Queensway and almost opposite Whiteleys. There is public transport nearby and it is about 300 metres from Hyde Park.

body: ... yes... if you are over 1,90 (over 6') you could be having some problems while having breakfast... or while walking upstairs... or... there were so many places where i felt I could be damaging my head! ;) Anyway.... the hotel is... average... appropriate for spending one or two nights... but I would be seriously considering different options if needing to stay longer (beds were quite uncomfy). I booked an individual room. It was clean... but smaller than expected. Also... everything looked worn (clean though). The area surrounding the hotel was very nice... lots of bars... tube quite close to the hotel... nice atmosphere... Definitively.. I would be choosing this same place for a short stay... but would be looking for something more comfy if planning to stay over two nights. WIFI worked ok (2.30 MBS) but if you need faster speed try NETGEAR with the same password provided by the hotel.

title: Once Off Stay
body: We stayed here early December for two nights (2 mothers, 2 daughters) on a short shopping break, Hotel is very central and bedroom was very clean but way too small as a family room. There was a terrible buzzing/gushing noise throughout the second night and very little sleep was had. My major concern was the corridors were soooo narrow and I would not like to be there if there was an emergency, also the lift was very slow and small. Staff were very helpful but never smiled - a smile cost nothing.

title: Great location
body: The best part of this hotel is its location. We stayed 3 nights. Very slow elevator; very small but clean bedroom, and very small bathroom; hanging space limited and access impractical. If you have a large suitcase, you'll have difficulty to open it (and not talking about having 2 suitcases!) since free space is really scarce. Breakfast is fine and not expensive (even better if it's included in the room price). When we asked the reception for a cab to take us to St Pancras Station, they said that a mini-cab would cost £23; we declined the offer and hailed a regular cab in the street - once at the station, the metered fare was £15 !

But the price for this hotel is still okay, and the location is fantastic with both Baywater and Queensway tube station just around the corner. But I would reccomend this hotel only if you are staying here for 1 or maximum two night.

title: Great location, good prices, NON-EXISTANT Wifi.
body: Like many of the reviews already state, this hotel is located in a wonderful location...lots of restaurants, two tube stations walking distance, Kensington and Hyde Park close by. Where things go wrong is in the apparently untrained Slavic reception desk staff. They are very unfriendly...never greeting guests when we walk in the door, one female actually rolled her eyes in response to my concern about cab pick-up, and they all tried to blame the non-working wifi on my "American computer." (an ipad2) In talking with other guests from Australia, Kenya and throughout the UK, we learned they could not access or stay logged into wifi either. Huge concern if needing to do business or just keep in touch with family and friends. The McDonalds down the road got our nightly visit to log on. Also, don't know if it was just our room, but we were only allowed one key (a real key at that) to use between my son and I. We had to coordinate our returns to the hotel and divvy up who got the key based on wo would be back first. Silly in this age. To sum things up, brilliant location, decent breakfast (albeit the same exact breakfast every day), inexpensive by London standards, SHODDY service and amenities.

title: nice hotel
body: We arrived at the hotel mid afternoon and was greeted by a very friendly helpful receptionist. Check in was very quick and ammenities were explained. Our room was a room for 4 people. However they were all single beds. The room was very clean and adequately stocked with tea, coffe and shampoos etc. The room was however very hot. A very short walk to Bayswater tube station on the district and circle lines and Queensway station on the central line, central London was easily accessable. We had a very comfortable nights sleep until 8.30m when we had a knock at the door by the chamber maids wanting to see if we were upto clean our room. After politely telling her we wasnt and returning to bed, we could hear her knocking on all the other doors in the corridor and then hoovering!! It was a Sunday and New Years Day...and slightly annoying. Breakfast was ok. Not much choice considering the price paid and no English breakfast available although we had been assured it would be when we checked in. Had English breakfast been available we noted a card on the table stating it was an extra £6.95p. This had definitely not been mentioned before!! Overall not a bad hotel, adequate for our first visit to the Lord Mayor of Londons new year fireworks party. Although many tube stations were closed on our way home and it did take us an hour and a half to walk back. This however does not reflect on the hotel, just bear it in mind if you are planning the same.

title: Suprised it's a BW
body: It's one of those standard size old English Hotels. Rooms are more like single rooms for double use. It's clean & it's continental breakfast is not that bad. As regards to the service with so many exchange students & immigrants working (not being racist) in the Hotel it can get difficult sometimes for the staff to understand what exactly you want. Location is good as it's a 2-3 min walk to bayswater & queensway stations that give access to central,circle & district line. Hotel has also free wifi , ask at reception. There is enough to do in the area ........ parks, restaurants, pubs ....... If you're young go for it, if middle age still go for it you like being squeezed ..... .

title: Small rooms but clean and friendly
body: I stayed here on business and being on my own was allocated a single room. I was shocked to see that paying guests get a room smaller than a prison cell. I was unable to change rooms as the hotel was full that night with other inmates, so I had to make do. The room was clean, although in need of updating, the bathroom was clean but again a little aged. The bed in my room was below the window, running along the side (i.e. the width of the room was the length of a single bed), because of this I shared part of my bed with the curtains hanging at the window - I wonder how many people had done the same, so I avoided them, sleeping on what remained of my side of the bed!. Next morning I went for breakfast to be pleasantly ignored by the staff, who were to busy . . mm . . just standing. For the second night I was moved to a larger single room - although again I would have killed any cats I attempted to swing, it was marginally bigger, but this room had been given a lick of paint and a new bathroom, making it all together, dare I say ok. This night I also had the bed to myself as it was situated along one of the walls. Overall for the price it was fair, and if you can wangle a larger room then you will be comfy.

title: Basic, Cheap & Clean
body: Was looking for a cheapish, clean hotel and chose this one. Hotel staff all foreign, but friendly. Rooms are clean including bathroom. Decor ok. Teas and coffee in room, towels etc. Our room was exceptionally warm even after i turned the radiator off. I had leave the window open all over the weekend (in October) ! The location is good as Queensway offers lots of eating establishments of nearly every nation on the planet. There are 2 very close tube stations nearby - Bayswater and Queensway. Right, here comes the bad bit- We had room and continental breakfast. We asked to upgrade to a full English expecting to have to pay the differnece between the £5 contenantal and £6.60 for the full English. We were told that we would have to pay the full £6.50. We waited for 45 minutes before giving up and walking out. As we walked out the breakfasts turned up. We sat back down and started to eat. After one mouthful and discovering the breakfast was cold we abandoned the breakfast and ate at one of the many aforementioned eating establishments close by. The hotel agreed not to charge us but offered no appology.

title: This was awful. Coming from someone who's stayed at some dumps.
body: Let me start by saying that I've traveled around the world. And I search for bargains and deals. I am almost never let down by the level of service and room I get. If I pay a dumply sum, I expect a junky place. But I believe I paid a nice sum. Not enough for marble floors, but enough for the common things we all want out of a hotel. Based on all the reviews I had read about prior to check-in, I was really expecting a good value for the money. Not so. It started in the lobby check-in, and went downhill from there. Initially, my husband and I were given a basement smoking room. I would not accept this and returned to the lobby. The young woman working almost acted as if she expected to see if that would fly, and immediately handed me a new key, to a room on the fourth floor. The room was small, but that's not a problem. Overall, it was attractive and tidy. The bathroom was clean and serviceable. Our first night I awoke, jet-lagged, and couldn't remember if I was in a hotel or my twenty-year old pull-out sofa. The bed pitched in the center, causing my husband and I to roll together constantly. It was probably the worst bed I've slept in since college. In the morning (with a clearer head and better lighting), we realized there was no roll for the toilet paper, there was no bath soap, and the wi-fi simply was not working in the hotel rooms. Two different calls to fix the wi-fi brought no resolution, only rude answers from the staff. We confirmed the touchy room wi-fi connection with some other patrons who were logged -on in lobby. One night upon arrival back at the hotel, the staff couldn't find our key. No problem. We just waited till they could locate it. But during that five minutes, the staff berated us, and insisted we hadn't returned it to them. Upon further examination, they found it had been placed in an incorrect slot. We didn't pay for the Ritz, but we did pay for wi-fi, a bed comfortable enough to sleep in, and common courtesy. Great location, but I would say they got lucky there. After 3 nights, we checked out and went directly across the street to the London House Hotel. Now THAT'S a great hotel. And a great value.

title: Basic hotel in great location
body: Staff on desk generally quite abrupt. Room was ready for us at 9am after arriving from long flight from Australia, so that was great. We had a family room for 2 kids and 2 adults. Really could have used a bar fridge in the room for cold drinks, fruit, etc, but the weather was cool enough for us to leave these things on the window sill to keep cool. Room was clean and tidy and bathroom was modern. Breakfast room was always busy over our 4 night stay, but always fully stocked with a nice range of food. Location was great, with shops, restaurants, tube and bus stops all within a 5 minute walk. Kensington gardens was also a short walk away which was great for kids to have a run and play.

title: Never again!
body: This had to be one of the worst hotels I've ever stayed at in London. It's location was great (right around the corner from Bayswater tube stop) but other than that it was fairly awful. The desk staff were the most unhappy group of people I have ever encountered. Not once did any of them smile at me. The staff that worked the continental breakfast was pleasant but had a very hard time keeping the buffet stocked and the tables cleared. The hotel was WARM. Ridiculously warm. You broke into a sweat as soon as you entered the lobby and the rooms were no better. The heat was off but it didn't matter. The windows only opened maybe 3 inches so that offered no respite. There was a fan in the closet, but in order to plug it in you had to move the desk to get to the plug, and even then I don't think you could have both the TV and fan plugged in at the same time. My bed was slanted so that I constantly felt like I was going to roll onto the floor. The shelf in the bathroom was also tilted so that if you put anything on there, it was likely to fall off, and, if you forgot to close the lid on the toilet, fall straight into the toilet (which you couldn't sit on without knocking the toilet paper off the holder). The showers were nice. Small, but I expected that. The noise from outside made sleeping next to impossible; maybe it wouldn't have been so bad if I didn't need to keep my window open (I was in room 319) but I did need the window open to try to alleviate SOME of the warmth. You also had to pay 1.50 for a 1/2 hour of internet access (I instead went to Whiteley's and paid 2 for internet access with a code that I could come back and reuse until my 2 hours were up). I usually stay at the Henry VIII Hotel which is a couple blocks away, but unfortunately they were booked. I was actually looking forward to my stay at a Best Western, thinking maybe that it would be a step up for me. NOT true in the least. I will never stay at the Phoenix Hotel again and will definitely be wary of ANY Best Western, no matter what country it's in.

title: Wi-Fi Internet Access is an Unusable Trickle
body: This is a perfectly nice budget hotel (I paid $85 a night on Expedia) -- room is cozy and clean (somewhat disturbing stains on bedspread, but otherwise fine), it's quiet at night, staff is nice, and location is great -- but the advertised free Wi-Fi access is so slow it's unusable. If Internet access is as important to your work as it is to mine, I'd look for another option. It's frustrating -- this is a very comfortable, pleasant hotel for the price, but dialup Internet speeds are a real problem when trying to stay up to date on work...

Would definately use again.

title: Small room but nice and quiet
body: The location is great. Next to a shopping center and 5-7 minutes walk from two tube stations, while Paddington is only a good 15 min walk away. The neighbourhood is nice with lots of restaurants. The hotel is quite old. I arrived at 10am and just wanted to store my luggage until check-in time. The very friendly girl at the reception then checked to see if my room was ready and 5 min after I could check-in and go to my room. The room was on first floor out to the street. The room was very small even for London standards and a little worn down. No aircondition but a small fan was available in the room. However the bed was comfortable and the room was sparkling clean for the whole period of my stay. The TV was very small but then again I did not go to London to watch television. The continental breakfast was fine, different kind of cereals, some fruit, toast, croissants, jam etc. In general the staff did not smile too much with the exception of the breakfast staff and the girl from the first day. One minor concern though - one day I forgot my room key and asked in the reception for help. The girl then gave me some kind of system key so I could fetch my room key. I guess she should have escorted me to my room in order to secure that I did not open other rooms. I did get my key and apart from this little incident I was very happy with my stay.

title: Location location
body: This was a great spot for quite retreat from a visit to London. It was a great base as it is a quick trip from the Heathrow Express at Paddington to the hotel. The Bayswater Underground Station is just around the corner. There is a large 3 story shopping centre 100 metres down the road. Plenty of restaurants, pubs and takeaways. There is nothing flash or fancy about the phoenix - it was really quite while we were there as the road out front had been closed and there was no traffic. The breakfast was a standard continental and was enough to start the day. Dining room staff were clean and efficient. We were early arrivals and late departures so got to use the lobby storage which seemed secure enough and was appreciated. The weather was fairly cool during our stay so didn't need air con but could see the rooms would warm up easily.

title: Reasonable and clean in a good location - good if you are on a tight budget
body: Overall this is not a bad hotel. We were (are at the time of this review) stuck in London and lost our reservation at the Sheraton. On a combination business trip/vacation with the family. Did not have high expectations based on the price. London is an expensive town and if you are on a budget the Phoenix is good. We did move to another hotel due to the concern related to personal belongings noted below – got tired of carrying around all of my work equipment (laptop/documents, etc) every time we left the room. The majority of our costs are covered by my work. If I were paying out of pocket for everything we would have stayed at the Phoenix. Positives: •The hotel is in a good location •Room was clean •The room with the loft area was a nice way to separate everyone for a little privacy •Laundry mat very close by •Bar in the lobby •Free wifi (very slow, but free) •Quaint and with character Negatives: •Staff were clearly stressed due to the volume of people - not horrible service, but not great. Called the front desk 3 times and no one ever answered. Walked downstairs and there were always 2 clerks sitting there. •Electricity for half of the room went out in the evening and had no lights in the bathroom (no windows) until the next morning. •No security for your belongings at all - nothing in the room and the doors have a single standard key (not electronic). Baggage storage area (pre check in) was open and I could have easily had my pick of luggage the number of times I went in and out. •Little bit of a walk to the tube - especially with young children. •No heat or AC to speak of and the building is stuffy - would think twice in the summer. Summary: If you have a tight budget this hotel will work. I mentioned security above only in reference to belongings – did not see any personal safety issues. Probably best for travelers who don’t mind a Hostel like feel for their stay and don’t have a lot of items to worry about. Would not recommend for the business traveler or someone with high standards for their hotels.

title: Small rooms in a great location!
body: Just stayed in the BW Phoenix hotel. I had a good trip, and compared to other hotels I've stayed in in London, the service was okay, the location was good, and rooms were as small as elsewhere in this pricecategory in London. However, there were some details which could have been better.... Reservations: Booked a package through a travel agency, so nothing special, but reservation was confirmed instantly. Location: het hotel is located in Bayswater, just off the larger street there with a lot of restaurants, fastfoodservice and small shops. It is a 3 minute walk from Bayswater tube station to the hotel, so excellent as well. Check-in/service/front desk: friendly personnel but average service at check-in. We asked for a twin room, but they asked us if we wanted to be "upgraded" to 2 single rooms located close to each other, but we declined this offer. They had all their twin rooms booked. However, there was no problem when we declined, we still got a twin room. For other questions the staff was helpful and tried their best. For example, when we had to print our boarding passes, it was no problem using the office computer, and the staff answered questions about shops and all. Room: we got a small twin room on the ground floor. The view was a wall, but I didn't come to London for my roomview, so wasn't bothered by it. As said the room was small, but I guess comparable in size with other hotel rooms in London in the same price range. But on the other hand, there were some details (or lack thereof) which could have given the room a boost. For example, there were no hooks on the wall to put a coat or clothing on. There was a closet, but that was set in the corner and it wasn't easliy opened or accessed. There were some free power outlets, but they were located behind the desk low to the ground, which asked for moving the desk in the small room, go on your knees and crawl under the desk to acces them....could have been better! the decor was a bit dated but okay. There was a watercooker and all there, as well as a tv. Overall, the room was average, but with minor changes could have been much better. If the lay-out or the furniture would have been designed to fit the room, it would have been an uprgrade for the room. I have stayed in small rooms before, but there the desk, closet and stuff was specially designed which made the room look bigger and nicer. There were 2 boxsprings, which I slept quite well on, but my friend didn't but I guess that is a personal taste thing! Temperature was good! Bathroom: clean, great shower, enough towels and apart from no space to put your toiletry bag (which wasn't that big a problem) no comments. Breakfast: average, but well maintained and friendly staff. There was bread (for toasting as well as rolls), croissants, meat, cheese, cereal, jam, chocopaste, and juices. For a small amount you could order eggs or an english breakfast. No frills in the breakfast room. Other amenities: there was a small bar in the lobby area, didn't use it but looked okay. Regarding the menu, it also served small "snacks" such as muffins. There were quite some seats in the lobby and it was decorated good. In the lobby was 1 computer with internet. The internet could be used for a small fee, speed was good. Overall: a great located hotel, with average, small rooms. It is comparable to other London hotels in the same price range, but with a good location. There were some minor points which were not that good, but mainly in the room amenities. As long as you go to London to see the city or at least not to be in the hotel room a long time apart from sleeping (which I guess most people are!) I think most people can handle the minor cons though, so I would stay there again!

title: Excellent location
body: The hotel is a good value for London. It is close to 2 underground metro stops and the Portobello Market was right around the corner. There are lots of restaurants and shops close by as well as laundry and postal facilities. The room we had was very reasonably sized and the bathroom was also bigger and more modern than expected. The hotel is clean. It is a hit and miss with the hotel reception employees. Some are great, others are not so nice and helpful. We did try the breakfast once or twice. Not very good, nothing what we expected. We are vegetarian and it really makes it hard to have a good breakfast when all you can eat is bread. Overall, I would probably stay at this hotel again.

title: tiny but worth it
body: I stayed here for 8 nights in early October, I had a single room on the 3rd floor facing the street. The hotel is nice, quaint could be used very easily. Starting off from the moment I got there things went well. The front desk checked me in, gave me my room key (an actual key, not a card) and the info so I could use the hotel's free wifi. When I got to the room it was tiny, I'm a big guy so it felt very tiny. I could easily touch two opposite walls standing in the middle of the room. The bed was a single but fairly comfortable. There is a small desk, tv and armoire in the room. The bathroom was just as tiny with a shower stall. Housekeeping did a good job keeping my room in order. The ladies at the front desk were helpful, some more than others. At the worst they were disinterested, they helped you if you asked for something but no friendliness. Most of the ladies were not like this. After the 2nd day I pretty much didn't have to tell them my room number, they would just hand me my key. Patricia in the office helped me out with my reservation and let me use the office computer to print off something. Breakfast, boring but plenty of it. I stuck with the continental breakfast and it was the same every morning, The ladies that worked down there were always polite. My only piece of advive is try to get a room that doesn't face the street, the hotel can't do anything about it but peopel are very loud as they go by and there is roadwork being done at the moment and I think they start about 8am. I would stay there again.

title: Back again and still ok
body: Had not been to the BW Phoenix , Bayswater, London for over a year. Found it 's still ok for me. Furniture may be dated to you taste. Carpet of my room (203) was showing wear/tear as did wallpaper. Shower/toilet room small. Room came with tv, hair-dryer, coffe/tea making facilities. Breakfast still ok. Staff still very helpful & kind. If unfamiliar with the hotel: breakfast-room can be full if you're not early. There's only 1 elevator so between say 08:00 and 10:00 when breakfast is served, guests are checking out, and rooms start to be cleaned, you may opt for the stairs. If you don't mind trafic-noice go for a front room with view of the private garden/park. I loved waking up in the morning hearing wind in the trees & birds singing. Hotel is within walking distance of Hyde Park, Queensway (plenty restaurants), Whiteleys shopping centre (small), Queensway tube station of the Central Line and Bayswater tube station (Circle & District). I'd checked the hotel's rates on Tripadvisor in euros using the currency selection field on the left side of Tripadvisor screen to see if a stay was affordable. The price shown on the screen while selecting the hotel & booking it through fastbookings.com, definitely did not tally with the bill I had to pay at the end of my stay. What was supposed to be the amount in euros turned out the be the amount in UK pounds. So travellers beware!

I'd checked the hotel's rates on Tripadvisor in euros using the currency selection field on the left side of Tripadvisor screen to see if a stay was affordable. The price shown on the screen while selecting the hotel & booking it through fastbookings.com, definitely did not tally with the bill I had to pay at the end of my stay. What was supposed to be the amount in euros turned out the be the amount in UK pounds. So travellers beware!

title: The service and hotel was good, great location and decent price
body: I chose this hotel mainly because the reviews were so consistent- This hotel is very conveniently located in Bayswater, near two subway lines and lots of shops and places to eat. (Avoid the nearby Pizza Hut, it's dreadful.) The staff was very helpful and the rooms were adequate. NOTE - if it is hot, you will suffer as the rooms are small and there is no air con. The service at breakfast was quick, the breakfast itself was good. Single rooms are VERY small, but overall the price is right, the place is clean and it is, most importantly, as described in most of the other reviews. No surprises, which is very important to me when I pay in advance for a room! I too had a multi level single room, but given how small the room was, it was actually nice to have the bed on a second level. The rooms on the bottom floors are probably even warmer, so request an upper floor would be my suggestion. This hotel is about a 6 pound taxi ride from Paddington, which is where the Heathrow Express brings you in from the main international airport, so that makes this even cheaper for those of us with too much luggage to take the tube.

title: Some flaws, but a descent experience
body: I stayed here for six nights. The room was tiny, about 7'x14, but I guess that's pretty common for a single in London. The room was clean and despite leaving the "do not disturb" sign up, there were clean towels waiting outside my door everyday when I returned. The free wireless Internet was perfectly serviceable, even with the low signal strength I was getting. The free continental breakfast was very good with a nice assortment of breads, rolls, cereals, croissants, fruit, yogurt and juices, and the waitstaff was very polite. Its a very short walk from both the Bayswater and Queensway tube stations, so that was convenient, and the nearby street had a wide variety of useful shops and economical ethnic cuisine and fast food. Now the flaws. Despite the cool March nights, the room was quite warm and I had to sleep with my window open to be comfortable. The problem with that is the hotel is adjacent to a very busy street, so loud passersby from the nearby pubs, bars and restaurants were quite annoying at all hours of the night, forcing me to sleep with earplugs. Also, they were renovating the room next to mine, and the work started at 8 A.M.. As that is when I was getting up anyways, it didn't present an issue, but someone that wanted to sleep in would have been disturbed. For what I paid, (less than $90/night) I would say it was a pretty good deal, but would be concerned about re-booking a room in warmer weather.

title: Basic, but comfortable
body: We stayed one night at the Phoenix before taking the Eurostar. We arrived in the evening and immediately had trouble with the staff. The receptionist barely spoke any English and did not think to tell my wife where our room actually was other than "you can't take the lift". When I returned to enquire I got the directions with an air of contempt from her. The room XIV between the ground and first floors, the bar tender whom we met on the way by contrast was very helpful. The room itself was comfortable and warm, and the bathroom was clean and unusually big for a London hotel. Bizarrely it had 4 single beds instead of the double we had booked, but the beds were clean and comfortable. The next morning the included breakfast was tolerable, but the staff again did not speak English particularly well.

title: Great Location and Fair Price
body: Just got back from a 6 day, 5 night stay at the Phoenix. In a word, the hotel and the rooms (we stayed in a room for 3 that included a queen bed and a single on the other side of the room) are basic. The rooms are relatively small and the hotel amenities are few. However, the rates are reasonable by London standards, the place is clean, and the included continental breakfast is decent. A recent addition is free wireless internet access throughout the hotel (you have to obtain a code and password from the front desk). Our bathroom also appeared to have been recently done over. A couple of negatives were the one very small elevator that seemed to have a mind of its own, the inside temperature of our room (it was always very warm and you can only open the windows about 7-8 inches), and the difficult time you have getting ice (you go to the bar and get a small cup filled). The biggest positive of this place is its location. It is very close to two tube stops (Bayswater and Queensway), which makes it very easy to get to many attractions such as the houses of parliment, big ben, the london eye, Thames River cruises, the Tate Modern, Buckingham Palace, the Tower of London, London Bridge, St. Paul's Cathedral, and more (you can get to most of these through the Bayswater stop on the "Circle Line" tube line). The hotel is also within walking distance to the Notting Hill area and Kensington Park and Palace. The Bayswater area also has many nice and reasonably priced ethnic restaurants and there is a shopping center just down the street where you can buy food, wine, beer (that's why we were looking for ice), snacks, and more. In all, I would stay there again and I recommend this place to anyone who values price and convenience over elegance and prestige.

title: Basic all the Way
body: I booked this hotel mainly for the location. It appeared to be very convenient to tube stations, shops etc., and I was not disappointed. The tubes were close enough even for a "non-walker" like me. The choice of restaurants and pubs was extensive. Now to the hotel itself: the best word is "basic". The single room I had was tiny (even by London standards), and the bathroom was reminiscent of a bathroom on board ship!! The carpet looked as though a good cleaning wouldn't hurt - but everything else was clean. I was amazed to discover one face cloth is issued to each guest ...... but you won't get another one unless you go to the front desk and request one!! There is an elevator, but it was out of service one morning which meant walking up and down five floors - not a good prospect four months after knee surgery!! The receptionists were very helpful and friendly. The free breakfast was very good, and the cooked breakfast was good though a bit high priced. Not a great hotel for a vacation, but if you are planning on being out all day and just need a place to sleep - it's not bad.

title: Good economy accomodation for short stay in Central London
body: When booking this Hotel, we were looking for no frills budget accomodation that supplied a good breakfast and central, yet quiet location. And that is essentially what we got. There were some initial problems with being allocated the wrong room and then we had to move as soon as cases were unpacked but otherwise this was an efficient stay. Unless you book a suite, it will be a very small box room however, not ideal for an extended stay. It appears that the bathrooms have been recently refurbished. Ideal location for all the usual attractions i.e. Hyde Park, Kensington, Knightsbridge, Kings Road, Oxford Street etc. 2 Tube stations very close by (Bayswater and Queensway). If you are coming to London to stay for an odd night for the theatre (as we did) etc. then this is an acceptable option. If your booking includes a complimentary breakfast, then please note it is a buffet/continential offering. You will have to pay an extra premium for a 'full english'.

title: Good location, convenient for tourists but loud
body: This hotel is in a great location, just a short walk from 2 tube stations and near fast food, touristy shops, a nice mall and cinema, and some good ethnic and authentic restaurants. The streets are loud, which is a pain because the rooms get quite hot (even in February with the heat off) so you'll need the windows open, there is no fan. The rooms are small by American standards and the pillows are lumpy, but the maids are accommodating, though I recommend you not have them clean your room as their version of cleaning is spraying some aerosol perfume all over the room. If you're just using this as a place to sleep and rest, it's fine. There's a quaint little bar, a very slow computer you have to pay to use, and a decent continental breakfast buffet included in the price. The location is the best asset, it's in a safe area close to 2 tube stops- about a 5 minute walk. It's also near Kensington Gardens. I'm not sure how this place would be in the summer, because I don't think it has air conditioning and it was unbelievably hot in the winter. The staff are friendly, you can leave your key at the front with them when you go out each day. They'll let you leave your bags with them if you arrive before check-in. Overall a decent but not luxurious place in a very good location, with some loud street noise that is especially easy to hear with the open windows (no screens either).

title: Bad, Bad, Bad
body: Do not believe the reviews below. Don't do it. We were scheduled to have a one-night stay at the Phoenix on our way back from Paris, and, based on the reviews written here, this looked like a pretty good hotel value. I can tell you it is not. The gory details follow below. Upon our Saturday night arrival, we were given a "ground floor" room (G-10, if I recall) that, when we opened the door, was notable for three things - (1) the worn, 1980's era 'Kansas motel' decor (including a bedspread that was clearly 15+ years old); (2) a wide open window, and (3) a horrible mildew smell that pervaded the room and made it smell like a crypt. Upon seeing this, we went back to the desk and asked to be switched to the other room. The woman at the front desk appeared irritated and told us there were no other rooms, but, after asking her to see the room roster she had in her hand, she conceded she had one other room. She then led us to another room (this time the 'basement' level) that may well have had the same mildew smell but for the acrid smell of cigarette smoke that had leeched into every square inch of the room. (Hoping to have us accept the room, she helpfully added "it has a flat screen!!!). We told her this was also unacceptable since we had booked non-smoking. Although she was clearly irritated, we returned to the front desk and asked to be switched to one of the upstairs rooms (of a guest that had not checked in yet.) She begrudgingly relented and pushed a key at us (the hotel does not have modern hotel locks or any modern conveniences - e.g. refrigerator, iron, safe) and sent us to the second floor. When we got there, we found the same decor as the previous two rooms, with a tiny TV (10" max) shoved in the corner of a worn out desk. (The TV had a melted lower corner, to boot). A small wardrobe and luggage rack were provided for clothes storage, but the remaining luggage had to end up on the desk. The shower and bathroom were clean (thankfully) but incredibly small (think medium closet size). One interesting feature was that the faucet had no mixing of hot and cold water (both came out of the same faucet as separate streams a few millimeters from each other). For electrics, only one outlet was readily available in the room to plug things in, so we couldn't power up anything other than one at a time. We put our things down, cleaned up for a bit, and went out to meet friends for dinner. When we returned, just out of curiosity, I pulled back the bed to see the sheets beneath the bedspread. The first thing I noticed were the multiple (7+) stains on the underside of the spread, including 3 that appeared to be old blood. The sheets were no better - although the sheets were made, there were hairs (not ours!) all over the sheets and pillowcases, making it appear that the bed had been slept in and then made. We called the night clerk (different than the first woman) and he agreed to get us new sheets and pillowcases but insisted on asking us "are you sure you didn't sleep in the bed yet?" (!!!) Shortly thereafter, we got the sheets, made the bed by putting the new sheets over the old sheets and the new pillowcases over the old pillowcases (I did not want to see what the mattresses and pillowcases looked like after seeing the underside of the bedspread), and slept a very uncomfortable 5 1/2 hours in a room with no air conditioning. The only pros, as I see it, of this hotel are the proximity to the Bayswater tube (about 1 1/2 blocks), free wi fi (you have to get a code from the front desk) and the good (included) continental breakfast. This hotel does not live up to the Best Western standard by any means, and do not be fooled by the name when you book. Also, someone here mentioned proximity to Paddington Station. It is not close, so don't book here if you think you can walk to Paddington for Heathrow Express.

title: Only for sleeping
body: First the pros: The location is good. West London, just by the park. Quiet side street with no disturbing noise compared to other London areas. The price is really good considering that breakfast is included. The bathroom is new and clean. The minuses: Interior is not horrible, but quite worn and you do not feel like walking around in your socks exactly. Colours are murky brown, orange red - and not the trendy kind either. The room first smelled of smoke so I asked to change. I wasn't greeted with a smile but they gave me another room without any fuzz. Outside the elevator was left a tray with half-eaten breakfast on the floor, and this was in the evening so it seems that there is no real inspection of the premises after the cleaning team has gone for the day. Rooms are normal in size, TV is very small and with bad reception. The cupboard smelled old dusty wood, wouldn't hang my best suit in there. The walls are thin, so if the guests next door are a noisy bunch you will hear them. All in all: You can't complain given the prize really, but I could only recommend this as an option to those spending only a few days and with a busy schedule so they don't have to spend so much time in the room. I'm sure there are better options if you are willing to spend a few more quid or if you are flexible with whereabouts you stay.

title: Good hotel but not for me!
body: I chose this hotel for business reasons working in London for a week in Feb. Its a real shame that it didn't score higher for me. I had stayed in some real horrors before and after a quick visit to the hotel, I seemed delighted to secure a room for a week. To be fair the hotel is clean and quite modern except for the lack of air conditioning which some of you may question as it was Feb, however, the weather was quite mild and the room was stifling. If my stay was taken in the summer then it would have been unbearable. I did seek the use of a fan, however, the hotel staff did not seem that bothered and did not provide one in the end. My colleague in another room did help out in the end. My room was a single room and it was on two levels, strange eh? The room was quite spacious for a single room and the bathroom was very clean with the shower being very hot when needed. The only problem I had was with the bed being very very uncomfortable and the tv being on the lower level away from the bed. This may seem daft but you were given a tiny chair to sit in front of it which can be very annoying after a while. The breakfast was very good with a very large selection overall. You can even upgrade to a full english breakfast for £6.50. Unfortunately I will not be choosing the hotel for the reasons stated above but the hotel is located in a great area with many pubs, shops and restaurants. It is only a five minute walk from two tube stations and Hyde Park. Oh yeah I secured this hotel for £60 a night, very reasonable for London.
text: Good hotel but not for me. I chose this hotel for business reasons working in London for a week in Feb. Its a real shame that it didn't score higher for me. I had stayed in some real horrors before and after a quick visit to the hotel, I seemed delighted to secure a room for a week. To be fair the hotel is clean and quite modern except for the lack of air conditioning which some of you may question as it was Feb, however, the weather was quite mild and the room was stifling. If my stay was taken in the summer then it would have been unbearable. I did seek the use of a fan, however, the hotel staff did not seem that bothered and did not provide one in the end. My colleague in another room did help out in the end. My room was a single room and it was on two levels, strange eh? The room was quite spacious for a single room and the bathroom was very clean with the shower being very hot when needed. The only problem I had was with the bed being very very uncomfortable and the tv being on the lower level away from the bed. This may seem daft but you were given a tiny chair to sit in front of it which can be very annoying after a while. The breakfast was very good with a very large selection overall. You can even upgrade to a full english breakfast for £6.50. It is only a five minute walk from two tube stations and Hyde Park. Oh yeah I secured this hotel for £60 a night, very reasonable for London.

title: good location but cramped
body: I spent 2 nights here on business, and on the plus side it is indisputably in an excellent location, close to tubes and buses and good shops. I felt safe there and going backwards and forwards as a single woman. It was clean too, and contrary to some reviews here, I found the staff friendly and helpful. So far, so good - and my room was cheap. Breakfast was adequate. On the minus side, my single room was absolutely tiny. I barely fitted into it! I had to juggle my luggage around and perch it on top of the wardrobe. The bathroom was miniscule. I am a small female - I can't imagine a big bloke coping with that room at all. The other major problem was the noise from other rooms. Guests were coming and going at all hours and with the paper-thin walls, you can hear every creak and door-slam. I didn't notice outside noise, but I was on floor four and as it was horrible winter weather, didn't open the window at night. It was the noise inside the place that was bad, the walls are soooo thin. I would only recommend it if the location means a great deal to you, you don't mind being cramped and you can put up with the noise... oh, and the lift is not up to the job - it's slow and there's only one, so often crowded at peak times. All in all, a claustrophobic experience!

title: You can do better elsewhere
body: I just returned from spending 8 nights at the London Phoenix Hotel, and my experiences echo those of “gottravelbug, Chicago, Illinois” (Dec 18, 2006). Don’t rely on the Best Western reputation here. The Phoenix isn’t up to that brand's standards. As every reviewer notes, the rooms are tiny. That’s not surprising in London, but it makes it important to use the space efficiently. The Phoenix flunks that test. For example, it wouldn’t be very costly to provide flat-panel, wall-mount TVs instead of the clunkers that take up half of the precious desktop, the only flat surface in the room. (And that only get a few channels, surely a disservice to the many non-English-speaking guests that the hotel hosts.) Most of the remaining desktop is taken up by a tea/coffee service. I didn't bring my laptop, preferring to shell out 50 pence per 30 minutes at a neighborhood cybercafe. I don't know where I would've put my laptop if I had brought it. Another example: closet space consisted of a standing wardrobe, about 3 feet wide and with cheap sliding doors that kept straying off their tracks. With so little clearance, hinged doors or pocket doors would have been much smarter. It contained only 4 hangers, inadequate for a scheduled 8-night stay. When I asked for more, the front desk grudgingly brought up 2 more. What is it with the clocks? Like travelbug, I found that mine needed a new battery. (Which the housekeeping staff provided, upon request….but why did we have to ask?) Maybe they figure the clock is invisible from the bed anyway, so who cares? Again, dumb design. (Memo: wear a watch in bed.) The room was very warm, even in October. I left the window wide open and tolerated the street noise. And the mosquitos. Yes, in October! (No screens. Dangerous, if you're traveling with young children.) The hotel encourages guests to reuse bath towels instead of requesting fresh ones every day. That's environmentally commendable (and I complied), but it would be pleasanter if there were more than a single narrow rod on which to hang used towels. “Travelbug” will be impressed to hear that my flimsy plastic bathroom glass was, indeed, replaced once during my stay. Décor was borderline shabby. Cleanliness and repair were marginal. The bathroom’s noisy exhaust fan, maddeningly, stays on long after the light is turned off. The one lift is inadequate. The breakfast room is unpleasantly crowded. The interior of the hotel is non-smoking, a plus. A consequence, though, is that smokers are almost always huddled on the entrance steps, so you enter the lobby through a cloud of tobacco smoke. The overwhelming impression is that the Phoenix is squeezing every pence out of this property, and dares its guests to ask for better treatment. I’m not some yahoo who’s never visited London before; this is my tenth trip or so. I stayed for 8 nights at the Phoenix only because I had prepaid through a booking service (big mistake) and dreaded the hassle of demanding a change. I would have been happier spending the same amount elsewhere, or spending less for a charming, cosmopolitan bed and breakfast (albeit with shared bath) that I’ve previously enjoyed greatly.

title: Reviews are Correct...average hotel
body: All the reviews are correct...some bad, some good, some great, but all of them tell the truth about Best West Phoenix. We booked our stay at the Best Western Phoenix Hotel through Hotels.com for our stay in Late September. When we arrived we were told they were overbooked and that they would put us up in their "sister hotel." I remember reading a review about this exact situation with this hotel so I stood my ground and said we were not leaving. They gave us a very small room, but we did not expect much since we knew before from this website what we were getting into. Advice for staying here: Don't except their invitation to stay at the other hotel, eat the wonderful breakfast before site-seeing in the morning and be prepared for very small accomodations. I would probably search for something better for the price next time I stay in London, but overall the location was great and we had an amazing time.

body: Hmm... how can one describe the noise level? It didn't seem to matter whether the windows were open or shut. We tried both, but the truck deliveries through the night were tiresome. Also, don't forget that the hotel does not have air conditioning which prevents you from closing the windows (noise) on a hot night.

title: Ok, but nothing more
body: Pros: - Cheap for central London - Conveniently located close to the Queensway and Bayswater tube stations and lots of restaurants, supermarkets, and stores. - Very quiet at night. Cons: - The hotel room was the smallest I have ever seen worldwide. I had a single bed, and it could barely fit in the room. The bathroom was closet-size. - The air condition in the bathroom is extremely loud and takes about 15 minutes to switch off after you have turned of the light in the room. - Breakfast was absolutely horrible - even for London. Far too many people crammed into a very uncharming basement and the food being of the absolutely cheapest variety bordering on the inedible. - The staff at the reception could not /would call for a taxi for us (when asked very politely.) All in all: An OK place to stay if you just want a bed to sleep in and nothing more.

title: Stay FAR Away!!
body: OK, it's been quite a while since I stayed here ... but looking at the pictures brought back the painful memories all too vividly. We booked this hotel through British Air, a 4 night layover en route to Cairo. It's location, the fact it was accross from a small park & the reasonable rate for London sounded pretty good to us. Standard room, 2 beds, nothing fancy. We were given a room with one double bed -- and that was all that would fit into that room! Thank goodness neither one of us is obese, or we wouldn't have fit on the toilet -- no joke intended. If you dropped the soap in the shower, it was all over! I lived in our 24ft trailer while we were building our home, and our trailer bathroom & shower were bigger than that bathroom. Believe me, I've travelled far & wide & I wasn't expecting luxury. This was just incredibly bad -- I had to crawl over my husband to get out of bed (or climb out the end of the bed & over a table) ... the door into the room only opened half-way because it banged into the "closet" (getting our suitcases into the room was a real treat) ... no place to put our suitcases except on the bed or in front of the bathroom door (we travel light with 24" bags). When we asked to be moved & said we had booked a 2-bed double room, we were told they could move us to a larger room but we would be charged extra (I forget how much it was now, but it was quite hefty). Let's just say the location isn't all that great to suffer through that again -- I'd definitely beware of this place!!

title: Don't Know We Got Bumped
body: I chose this hotel because the reviews seemed good and there seemed to be lots of amenities in the area, however, upon arrival we were told that the hotel was over booked (despite us having a reservation for more than a month) and that they were putting us up at a sister property. This seemed to be a normal experience for them so beware! The sister property, John Howard, while reasonably nice, was in the middle of nowhere so we spent all of our time trying to get places. If you book at this hotel and they try to bump you to the John Howard and you don't have a car, unless you're a marathon walker, insist that they honor your reservation!

title: Nice little hotel, but overpriced
body: We stayed at the Phoenix with a group of college students in May of this year while on a long weekend in London. While the rooms were quite small, the location was convenient--just around the corner from the Bayswater Underground station with many conveniences nearby, yet in a fairly quiet and very attractive neighborhood. The windows opened to let in fresh air--always a plus--and the free Continental breakfast was quite plentiful, including fruit, cheese, cold cuts, along with the usual breads and juices. We were unable to access the in-room internet service, despite instructions from the front desk, but a computer is available in the lobby--for a price, and quite slow. However, the bathrooms were of a good size and quite clean. Water pressure was good and hot water was plentiful. All in all, this was a nice, "moderate" hotel at luxury prices.

title: Sardines On Toast
body: We arrived at the hotel late evening after booking through Hotels Com earlier that day, to be told there were no rooms available . Having been debited for the £150 accomodation (cost for two nights) we were less than impressed. Seemingly the hotel had not closed off availability and the provider sold the room in good faith . The initial attitude at reception was I have no rooms , end off. We were then told of a close by sister hotel but that would be quite a bit more , with Hotels Com unwilling to comit to any subsidy, presumably as it was not their fault. Best Western refused to subsidise the difference, though eventually offered a room descibed as a double yet only used for single occupancy, their only concession was free breakfast. Well at 11pm tired and desperate to secure a bed we elected to stay. Probably a mistake the room offered 124 was just able to accomodate a queen size bed and there was a large mount of damp evident on the walls. The next day we were given room 211 seemingly standard fare , but this was only marginally bigger and so warm that we sought soft drinks at 4am. Breakfast was good in terms of food , but the tables so close and so packed it was uncomfortable . All in all despite a further 10% discount due to my protestations I left the hotel thinking it was quite terrible and not what Best western would be proud of. the plus side was location and the bathrooms which were good. Downside incompetant / uninterested reception staff , rooms that were a disgrace and a hotel existing only on location & unsuspecting foreign tourists who presumably leave with a very poor impression. Advice stay away and pay a little more.

title: Very small single rooms
body: The Hotel Phoenix is in a great location in an ecclectic part of Bayswater. It is convenient to two tube lines and there is a bus stop across the street that, with transfers, can get you into central London. The staff was very friendly and helpful, the service was great and the breakfast was more than adequate. HOWEVER, the room was the smallest I have ever experienced and I had difficulty in just moving about (5' 9" 175 lbs). Also the room was hot (January 31st). While the hotel is rated 3 Stars, I would put the room at 2 Stars. If you leave early in the day and get back at late night, the room is OK but do not plan to invite friends in for a drink because they will not be able to get into the room because of the small size!

title: Unless You Don't Mind Sweating, Don't Stay Here
body: I booked this hotel on the basis of the Best Western name through British Airways, knowing that British Airways usually has standards for the hotels for which they sell booking. I like to stay in Hyde Park by Lancaster gate but read the tube station would be closed in October and was afraid it might extend into December. I was very disappointed. In the 12 hotels I have stayed in in London, this ranks #11, just above one independent budget hotel I stayed in on Sussex Gardens near Paddington Station. I stayed in a single room. The room was very small and slightly shabby. The room was clean, carpeting clean, but there were spots and marks on the wallpaper. There was a small wardrobe at the foot of the bed with 5 hangers and half of it taken up with a shelf with a coffee/tea service on it. There was a small desk with two small drawers which had a small TV on it and telephone. There were no sattelite channels on the TV. There was a rack next to the desk for a suitcase. There was a clock on the wall above the door which was not working. The bathroom was tiny. The toilet was in a niche in the wall with about 2 inches on either side. I had to sit slightly sideways on the toilet because of the toilet paper roll just about overlapping the seat. The toilet faced the walk-in shower (which had no shelf in it), and in between against the wall was a sink with no room between with a small glass shelf above the sink. When I arrived, there was a plastic glass wrapped in cellophane with the Best Western logo. This glass was never changed throughout my 10-day stay. I probably should have thrown it away and maybe would have received a new one. There is no way you can dry off from showering with the door closed. The really terrible, unbearable thing about this hotel was that it was miserably HOT in DECEMBER. The radiator in the room was not on. The radiator in the hall was warm, so I don't know where all the heat was coming from. I spoke to several other people who said their room was very warm and they had to leave the window open. Looking up from the street, one could see many windows open. The problem with this was that you could hear all the street noise, which continued on to all hours of the morning. The hotel had a linen delivery at 1:00 a.m. right out in front of the hotel in front of my room with people unloading the truck talking loudly. Where is the consideration for hotel guests? I think cabs used this street to turn around to return to the main street. One night as I lay awake, I could hear snoring coming from the room next door. I received 6 nights for the price of 5, so the price was very reasonable, but in the end, you get what you pay for!! If you can't deal with these discomforts, spend a little more and stay in a better hotel in a nicer, more quiet area.

title: A bumpy start but things improved
body: My fiancee and I stayed at the Phoenix from September 9-14. We requested a non-smoking, double room, only to find out upon arrival that we had a smoking room with two single beds...in the basement (you couldn't even use the sink because it had a glass shelf covering most of it - - doesn't make washing your face very easy!!) They were completely booked the first night but promised to move us to a different room the next day. They did as they promised and we were moved up to the second floor the next day (a big improvment!) The only problem we encountered during our stay after that was on the third night when we got back to our hotel room to find a note in the shower saying that we could not use it. We inquired with reception and they said the problem would be fixed the next day. When we got back the next afternoon, all of the rooms had signs on them saying "do not use, chlorination in effect". Again, we inquired with reception and they said that it would be safe to use the water in about half an hour but they would notify us. title: It is clean and central
body: Just back from a four night stay at this hotel. The major attraction of this place was it's location, as mentioned previously it is only a few minutes walk from either Bayswater or Queensway tube stations, from either of these anywhere in London is readily accessable. The hotel is clean, the rooms are small and the breakfast is good, but I thought paying £6.50 extra for the english breakfast was a bit much. The staff are good enought to deal with and while there isn't a safe in the room one is available at the reception area. We checked in early in the day and there is storage for your bags 'till you get back and are allowed into your room. The area is filled with multi cultural dining, so the ambitious people get plenty chances to try something new. We had a top floor room overlooking the square and at night people going home at 1am seemed noisy. The heat in the room was overbearing, the building needs air conditioning, I can understand how the people who stayed there during the heat of the summer must have felt. We had to sleep with the windows open fully, which didn't help with the noise form passers by or traffic. Yes we would stay there again, simply because it is so easy to get to the hotel from Heathrow and the proximity to the tube stations and Kensington Gardens makes it worth while. It is a great base from which to tour London.

title: Good value for money
body: Booked 5 nights at this hotel via BA website. The non-smoking single room faced the street and was tiny and the bathroom even tinier. The first night the tiny TV didn't work and the showerhead in the ti... (OK, OK you guys get the picture) shower sprayed water everywhere except on my body. Both the problems were fixed promptly the next day. The street can get noisy (conversations carried quite loudly at night into the room even with the window closed) so I would suggest booking a room away from it if you want some peace and quiet. Add to that the thin walls and you hear a lot of door banging and conversation. The decor is showing signs of wear and tear. The hotel is located off busy Queensway road with a lot of ethnic activity and has a host of Middle Eastern, Thai, Chinese, Indian and other take-out/eating places (my favorite was Nando's Portuguese BBQ about 5 minutes walk away). The breakfast was basic and I would imagine it was meant to be tucked into to tide you over your morning activity. On the plus side is the hotel's location (a few minutes walk to the tube and to Kensington Palace/Park), friendly staff and reasonable value for money. Recommended.

body: I stayed for 4 nights in August 06; the hotel is very well located (2 tube stations + Paddington Train station nearby, a shopping mall Whiteley´s just around the corner).
