Also, the water pressure was absolutely horrible. But for 4 nights it was bearable. The breakfast was nice and the staff was friendly, so overall I was satisfied. But I doubt I´ll go back, especially in the summer!

title: Would recommend the Phoenix
body: My husband and I stayed at the Phoenix for 3 days this past July (2006). Based on reviews on this site, I was extremely impressed with the hotel for its price range. The Phoenix is very convenient with the Bayswater tube stop about 1.5 blocks fro the hotel, along a nice street with shops and restaurants. Upon arriving in the morning, we were able to store our bags until our room was ready, however it's not an extremely secure location, but everything worked out ok. We didn't get back to the hotel until late that evening after sight-seeing and found our room very warm. This hotel doesn't have airconditioning but they had placed a fan in our room already. Our one big problem during our stay was that the bathroom wasn't cleaned to my standards and even had the last person's soap still in the tub. Otherwise things were ok. The room was big for London, the street noise wasn't too bad with the window open, the breakfast was more than enough (rolls, croissants, toast, cheese, ham, cereals, fruits, juice, coffee/tea) and the people were pleasant for the most part. They do have internet available in the lobby for a fee which helped us with some last minute planning. Overall I think the Phoenix is overpriced, but actually a deal for London. Would stay there again if looking for that price range.

title: Good location, rather noisy
body: After reading all the good reviews here, I decided to book this hotel. Normally I stay in the Comfort Inn Earl's Court but that hotel was fully booked. I found the two hotels very similar. The hotel is situated in a nice block, in an old building. The street is a nice side street from Queensway road on which you can find many local shops, cafe's and restaurants. Also the Whiteley shopping mall is just around the corner, which is very handy. On the third floor of the mall there are some restaurants that looked okay. I didn't try them, only went there to check my e-mail on an Easy internet computer (1 pound for an hour). The Bayswater underground station is only a few minutes walking. I had a single room that was quite small, but that is often the case in cheaper hotels. The bed was comfy. The room faced the street which meant that you could hear the people coming back from the pubs, but it was not too bad. The walls though were very thin. Perhaps my neighbours were just very loud, but it sounded like they were in my room. The bathroom was small but okay and there were coffee and tea making facilities. The only thing I missed was a safe (there is one in the earl's court hotel). The hotel could do with some modern decoration I thought, but it didn't bother me. I liked the layout. In some (budget) hotels you get lost easily because of all the corridors, but in this hotel it's very easy to find your room. I wouldn't mind staying in this hotel again, because it is very difficult to find a decent, clean hotel in a safe area very close to a tube station that isn't extremely expensive. But perhaps it's best to take some ear plugs with you, just to be on the safe side.

title: Better spare your money
body: We spent a day and a half in London, and we stayed at the Best Western Phoenix hotel. The fact is that this was not a 3 star hotel as easyjet and hotelopia claimed it to be. I even wonder why Best Western chose this building to be a member of their family. The space given to us as a double-room was exactly the size of an almost double bed. You open the door and actually step on the bed, there was no more available space even to stand and get dressed. The restaurant was down at the lower basement with some windows protected by iron bars and we had to wait for almost half an hour in the queue in order to be seated and have breakfast, if someone can call breakfast the poorest buffet i've ever seen. We certainly felt like prisoners going from the cell (- so called room) to the dinning area (- so called restaurant) to have our portion of bread and water (- so called breakfast). The floor was covered by wall-to-wall carpeting and was squeaking on every step giving the impression that on any minute you were going to fall in some hole covered by the carpeting. Not to mention the odour in the corridors and the room. Ok the location was good, near the underground, peaceful neighbourhood and we had room service and clean towels every day but thats it. As a conclusion i don't recommend it, didn't deserve the money spent. Definitelly won't go there again and you shouldn't too if you respect yourself.

title: Average hotel
body: I went to England for two weeks, for all but 4 of the days I was elsewhere besides London and stayed with friends of mine. But I needed a hotel for the first and last two nights of my trip. The first two I stayed in the Thistle Charing Cross which was much better than the Phoenix cost twice as much. It probably had my expectations higher. I got to the Phoenix and realized the location just wasn't as great. I preferred being in the west end. With the Phoenix you had to take the tube to get pretty much everywhere. One of my biggest problems with the location was that I wanted to go to a club or bar in Leicester Square at night however because the tube stops running at around midnight I would have to find a taxi and pay a lot or take the bus back. I couldn't just walk back in less than 5 minutes like I could at the Charing Cross. Otherwise the location was fine because the tube got you anywhere. As for the room, I got a single room. It was small, but that's fine, I was a solo traveler so I didn't need huge. The bed wasn't great, just average. The room was on the warm side even with the window open. It was pretty clean though. The free breakfast was average...better than nothing as it had breads with all sorts of spreads, cereal, coffee, ham, and some fruit. One thing I noticed is that all the staff was foreign whereas at the Thistle many were British. So some couldn't speak english well. The lady at checkin was rude. So service wasn't great. However, I only paid about $150 for two nights here. So I can't complain, it was a decent place to stay and if I were to come again and couldn't get the Thistle for that price, I might stay here.

title: Not Good at all......
body: We stayed in 2 rooms here in November. The good news first- The location is awesome, very close to the Tube and a lively neighborhood just a block away. Other reviews have it well chronicled here. The free breakfast buffet is adequate, but very boring after a couple of days. The pub /lounge is good, comfortable, affordable, and friendly. They offered complementary snacks during happy hour, which was nice. The bad news- They really messed up the reservation and gave us the wrong room, so we had to move the next morning. They charge absolutely criminal rates on phone calls ( 1 pound for a 10 second call to an 800 number). We were using several kinds of 800 number phone cards, and had to pay an additional $100 in calls when checking out. They charge a very high price for internet access in the public lobby. $3.00 for 20 minutes is not a good deal. They claim to have "satellite TV", but the TV's in both rooms only received 7 channels each, while the TV in the pub got several hundred channels. They claim to have "concierge" service, what a joke. All of the deskstaff was cold, pompous, and unfriendly. The maid service was lousy, they only emptied the trash cans, ignoring used coffee dishes, empty bottles, etc. They didn't replace coffee cups, spoons, etc, they let trash pile up for days. The heaters in the rooms were very hot and couldn't be turned off for some reason. We were forced to constantly have the windows open (in Nov) to keep from sweating. The shower water was scalding if you weren't very careful with the controls. I think the value for this hotel was decent, but don't expect too much, and you will be happy here.

title: Good Hotel for Money
body: Just returned from London, spent 6 nights at the Phoenix and for the most part we were pleased. Yes the rooms are small, but I understand most are in the area - the rooms are clean and cosy! No AC but open the window during the day and use the fan at night, if a hot day in Summer, get a hotel with AC if you must. Location is excellent, very multi-cultural, close to the tube, and shops, pubs, and lovely indian food. Staff are ok, english is not their first language but no problems to report. The pillows were very hard, we asked them to change ours for us and they did. The reason the pillows were hard is that they are new pillows - good sign. Nice little Bar area and after a long day, a cold beer is just what you need to relax from touring. Food - the continental breakfast is one of the best I've seen - better than most in Canada or US. Lots of selection, and the tea is great. Price of hotel is good, we would have preferred AC, I guess we are spoiled. One final note, the bathroom is small, but modern and managable, if you plan to spend a lot of time in the room don't stay here pay several $$$ more or stay home. Good value for money. Would stay again.

title: You get what you pay for
body: The main advantages of the Phoenix are that it is inexpensive and that it is conveniently located. Anyone who stays here expecting anything other than a typical London budget hotel will probably be disappointed -- the rooms are small, the breakfast is minimal, etc. The bathroom in my room was quite adequate by London hotel standards. I found the staff to be quite pleasant. I stayed there in March, and would probably be willing to stay there again if I were travelling to London on a budget -- but since the rooms are not air conditioned, I'd probably think twice about staying there in summer.

title: Reasonable price made it a good choice.
body: I stayed here for three nights at the end of March in a single room. I have stayed in London a few times before and the room size seemed comparable to other single rooms I have stayed in. I choose this place based on the reviews from tripadvisor and because I found a good rate for the place on a London hotels web site, 49GBP per night. I had to laugh when I returned home and saw that some of the reviews that have been a bit more mixed in recent weeks. As I was having similar thoughts about the hotel. Here are what I thought were the best points. Great location, close to many shops and resturants. I felt safe walking at night back from the tube to the hotel as there were lots of people still walking the streets, even as late as 11pm. The room seemed clean and as I mentioned earlier, the price was very good. The room appeared clean, ironically, the wall clock in my room also needed a new battery. The bathroom was small but typical of London. I did, however, get sprayed a few times by the facet sink, as it could only be turned on very lightly, almost a dribble, or the water bounced off the small sink and hit the person in front of the sink. While breakfast was free, it was pretty bland and appeared of low quality. And the breakfast staff seemed overwhelmed and while not unpleasant, they did seem joyless in their work. I would stay here again if I was able to secure a reasonable rate but at the same time will keep an eye out for other possibilities. Perhaps back to bed and breakfasts, once a person has enjoyed a well cooked English breakfast it is hard to not want the same quality again. But I would recommend this hotel, especially for women travelling alone who need a budget choice.

title: Acceptable and satisfactory
body: My wife and I stayed in this hotel for three nights in December 2003 and had a good time. Yes, the elevator had problems when we were there. Bad start, but it got better. We got here on a cold, rainy day and were happy to find a warm hotel with friendly staff. When we got to our room, we found it to be clean and fine. Nothing fancy, but no complaints, either. The room was kind of stuffy, but an open window took care of that. Heater worked great and we had no cigarette smell troubles. The room was fine for two people, not big, but not bad either. No airco, but who needs it in December. The clock didn’t work, but who cares? The colour TV worked fine, but who cares when you’re in London. If you are in London as a tourist for a couple of days and can take a few setbacks here and there, it is a fine place to stay.

title: Not so bad, not so good
body: I stayed here for 7 nights. Read the reviews on this site before booking and found them mostly accurate, if a little optimistic. I was travelling alone, and booked a single room. Yes, it was tiny! Wee! Miniscule! Carpet was threadbare and stained in places, water damage to wallpaper and carpet in one corner. Although I had requested a non-smoking room, my room had an ashtray in it (although it didn't smell of smoke) and my neighbors smoked. My room was on the fourth floor, with a lovely view over the square. Mostly pretty quiet at night, although since I live in a big city I might not be as sensitive to noise as others. The room was extremely clean ... and I'm picky! Bathroom (also tiny) was spotless and the shower had good water pressure and ample hot water. I had no trouble getting an extra pillow and batteries for the TV remote. Never ate breakfast, so can't comment on that. Elevator is a little scary (clunky). No peephole or deadbolt on room door. Location is good; close to two tube stations and within easy walking distance of tons of restaurants and shops. Would I stay here again? Yes, but if I could find something better maintained at the same low price, I'd stay there instead.

title: Convenient but Lacking Big Time
body: I stayed at this hotel for five nights the week before Easter, booked by a travel agent. After reading the reviews here I thought it would be a great hotel. Although a convenient location, great shops, and the tube so close, the hotel lacked quite a bit. I've stayed in other London hotels, and yes there are the horror stories, but some of these reviews pump this hotel up more than it deserves and can misdirect someone. There were two of us and a teenager in a room that overlooked the side roof area with a dismal view of London and the hotel pipes and no where to put luggage became very frustrating. The small loft area was really a nusiance. Although clean, (even though the maid cleaned in her barefeet) it was tiring to leave notes to keep the screenless windows locked and shut and not wide open. Even that didn't help, and every day we would return to wonder if our belongings were gone. I finally put a travel lock on it so she would stop opening them. Doors paper thin and two nights running a group had their doors open into the hallway directly across from us, smoking and carrying on till 4AM, & knocking on our door. Don't bother calling the front desk, seems they think you are the bother. And if you need an electrical outlet to charge anything, well, expect one usuable outlet which you have to crawl under the desk to get to after unplugging the fading black and white TV . The daily breakfast gets old after the first day, no changes, and not much choice. (Great pastry shop around the corner, and plenty of restarants in the mall across the street.) Elevator broke two times we were there, and yes, it was when we needn't it to carry the luggage up the stairs. Some staff were helpful, however, don't ask for an iron, because you have to pick it up at the desk, and the cord is so frayed that using it looked hazardous. I thought I caused a meltdown when I asked for a battery for the one wall clock in the room that I guess hadn't been running for awhile. I also had to bring that down and put it back up myself. They have no means ( or they tell you that) to hold luggage, and if you arrive when a tour group does, there is no room in their small lobby to even stand. The hotel is inexpensive by London standards, however, they will up the rate on weekends on you even if you have a package deal with a travel agent. We checked out a day early, drove to Bradford on Avon, and stayed at a bed and breakfast that was beautiful. Cheaper, cleaner, safer, and the staff much better. Sometimes spending the few extra dollars to upgrade to a safer and fresher hotel is worth it when you are exhausted and traveling with a teenager. If in a pinch, this hotel is worth the convience, however, any more than two days and it becomes downright depressing.

title: Best stay I've had in London, excellent gluten free breakfast available
body: I stayed at the Phoenix hotel for four nights and I had a really great experience. All of the staff were so so friendly, so polite and so welcoming! Literally every single one of them. I booked last minute and they were so accommodating, and considering I did book so last minute the price was reasonable. The bedrooms were fine, simple, comfortable beds, great shower. It has everything you need. On some of the nights it was really windy and I was on the fourth floor so the windows were rattling all night long, meaning I didn't get much sleep. However the second night when it was really windy I just jammed some card in the windows and that stopped the rattling - problem solved. The breakfast was absolutely fabulous. I am gluten free and quite used to there being limited selection at breakfast buffets but they had an entire gluten free selection and assortment of so many different kinds of foods and even a separate toaster for gf bread! I was highly impressed. The coffee was fab too. The housekeeping staff were also lovely and did a great job. I left out quite a lot of valuable items when I was in a rush and they were all still in place, so no one has to worry about anything going missing. I'll be back! oh yes and I had an art exhibition so after my exhibition they even let me store some of my things until I checked out so that my room wasn't too cramped! 20/10 service and experience with the staff! Location - one of the best in London. Absolutely loved the location, it's so stunning there and so safe, which is something not to be taken for granted in London. The atmosphere was quiet but welcoming, peaceful, friendly and in general great.

title: Good
body: I had a very pleasant stay at this hotel. The location is excellent and the hotel itself is beautiful, clean, and very well maintained. My room and bathroom were spotless, and I really appreciated the daily housekeeping service. Early check-in was also a big advantage and made my arrival much easier. The staff were always very kind, helpful, and patient. Even though my English is not perfect, communication was never an issue, which I truly appreciated. I also appreciated the desk fan provided in the room, which was very helpful during the warm weather. On the other hand, there were a few things that affected the comfort of the stay. The main issue was the lack of proper ventilation, as the window could only be opened slightly, which made the room feel quite stuffy, especially in the mornings. Noise insulation could also be improved, as sounds from neighbouring rooms and the corridor were quite noticeable. The bathroom was very clean, but rather small, and I would have preferred a handheld shower instead of a fixed overhead one. Overall, I really enjoyed my stay and would happily recommend this hotel. Despite the minor issues, I would definitely consider staying here again in the future.

title: Lovely hotel, great staff and perfectly situated
body: Stayed here 4 nights just before Christmas with 2 adults. Lovely hotel with a warm and cozy atmosphere. Very friendly reception, housekeeping and breakfast staff. The room we had was spacious and, most importantly, very clean. The mattresses were slightly above average hardness, so they should be comfortable for most people. The shower worked well. Enough power outlets in the room to charge our phones and powerbank. Note that for EU plugs you need an adapter. Breakfast was as expected, with all "standard" food and drinks available. The hotel is situated near three Underground stations (Bayswater, Queensway, and Royal Oak), so perfectly situated for trips into the city. Notting Hill and Hyde Park are even at walking distance directly from the hotel. For a future visit to London I will definitely try to book this same hotel.

title: Amazing position in central London, it would only be nice to have any vegan alternatives for breakfast.
body: Phoenix Hotel is in a wonderful position to explore London - midway between Tube stations Bayswater (Circle line) and Queensway (Central line). Walking distance from Kensington Gardens, which becomes Hyde Park after the canal and the bridge. Close to shops and restaurants. My friend and I booked two single rooms and they were clean, comfortable, with everything necessary. The staff were generally kind and supporting, except from a lady to whom I asked if they had bananas for breakfast and she was very sharp and just said no. On a slightly negative note, as breakfast is included, it would be lovely to have some more vegan options. I had to go with bread and jam, which was fine for a few days, though I would have appreciated some more fruit choice (bananas, red berries, dried fruits, for example) or some oatmeal to prepare with the Hotel's coffee. Thank you so much if you will consider to make only some little adjustments to meet everybody's requirements. Overall, I plan to return when I go back to London.

One star deduction: the double bed can be used by two people of normal build, but if one person is a bit wider, it becomes difficult. title: A friendly and welcoming Hotel near Hyde Park
body: Once again this Hotel's lovely staff made me feel at home in one of my London trips. I had purchased an accommodating double room, which, as it was on the ground floor was very convenient to a creaky 69 year old like me. I find the location so close to Paddington Station, makes my trip up from the West country easy and I particularly value the parks and Hyde Park and Kensington Gardens are very close. The members of staff remembered me which is very warming and they made haste to show me a jacket that had been left behind and wondered if it could have been mine. This is part of why I have been staying here for the best part of 40 years.

title: Excellent value for money, including for solos
body: I have stayed at the Phoenix a number of times. It is excellent value for money; especially for me as a solo traveller with your singles and small double rooms. The communal areas are smart and the rooms, although small, are clean and comfortable, with a good shower and hairdryer. The addition of tea tray, shower gel, shampoo, tissues etc is a bonus. Although no air con, an electric fan helped when it was very hot. Only minus is the lack of air con and no safe. I highly recommend your hotel Your staff friendly and helpful and having a manned desk is excellent. The addition of a simple included breakfast, check in from 1pm and the ability to leave luggage before or after are also much appreciated. The location is excellent, a quiet turning but near shops, cafes, Hyde Park and 2 tube lines. The area feels safe as it is busy.

I sincerely hope the high standard remains, as we’re already planning to return next year.

title: Great hotel!
body: My stay at the Phoenix Hotel in May 2025 was excellent. The hotel has a great location: It is close to Queensway, where there are shops, restaurants, markets, pubs, pharmacies, and two subway stations, Bayswater and Queensway. It is also very close to Hyde Park. The room is very comfortable and clean. There is no air conditioning, but this wasn’t a problem for me. The breakfast is very good, with ham, salami, cheeses, eggs, fruits, cereals, bread, and croissants. And a coffee machine with many options. The entire staff is welcoming, kind, and polite. And also very important: the hotel has a luggage room to leave your luggage until check-in and after check-out. I recommend the Phoenix Hotel as accommodation in London.

title: Hotel in a quiet area just next to public transport , shopping and restaurants
body: I would especially mention the service level from the hotel staff, who did everything to come up with solutions to the issues that occurred. First we had a “basement room” which was very nice and fulfilled our needs. Outside the window there was a lamp shining and on our request the staff looked into to turn it off the day after. On our second day we were offered another room on the 2nd floor which was perfect for us travelling with a soon teen. Unfortunately two days later there was a water leak and we had to leave for a new room, which first could be ready at noon, so meanwhile we had a temporary single bed room. Our overall 4th room was in ground level which was as all the other rooms very good. Cleaning service was good, every day change of towels and clean up. Breakfast was fine, continental, and you could order English breakfast as well. Reception service was good, fast checking in and out and always helpful and listening to what we bring to their attention. Overall great services and a very good location in a very tranquil area, 3 minutes from the tube and bus, and restaurants and shopping just around the corner. This is a hotel we surely should be coming back to when we visit London again. Best regards Jakob

title: Great quality-price ratio for friendly and excellently located hotel
body: Very good pr ice-quality ratio, excellent location in the city and compared to nearby public transport stations. Staff was kind and helpful at all times. Would recommend and would consider returning. I had a single room on the top floor, it was small but adequate - comfortable bed, clean room, relaxing view on the street and adjacent park. Soundproofing could be improved with regards to noises coming from the hallway, especially considering that my room was the one directly facing the elevator and a lot of people passed by it. Very good cleaning service performed daily with towels and toiletries changed day-to-day. The shower mat could be cleaned a little better on the underside, where mould was starting to form around the suckers, but that didn't prevent its use. The angles of the shower frame itself showed signs of limestone. Breakfast offer was nice, continental with a good range of salted and sweet options. I was expecting to find an English breakfast option upon additional payment, though, but it seemed it was not contemplated in any way despite the hotel key card having it listed (not ticked in my case, so I wasn't expecting it - I'm just pointing this out as I found this detail to be a little perplexing). Despite these small notes, as I said before, my impression was definitely positive and I would certainly consider returning.

The staff were friendly and knowledgeable about the local area and extremely courteous, the accommodation clean and the property overall was very well looked after. Despite the hotel being very busy on our last day, we had no problems getting a table for breakfast, and check out was quick. We were also able to leave our bags for collection later which meant our last day (a beautiful warm day) could be spent strolling nearby in both Kensington & Hyde Parks. If back in London we would defo be back at the Phoenix!

title: Another great stay
body: Whenever we visit London we have stayed at the Phoenix Hotel and that’s been the case for years. We have always been very happy with the room we’ve been allocated ( although the rooms can be hot sometimes but that’s no real problem) and find them very clean and well serviced. The reception staff are so welcoming, kind, friendly and helpful with sound customer care skills and always there for all the people who stay at the Phoenix Hotel. Thank you so much to all the reception staff who were on duty during our stay from 7th to 9th July. The continental breakfast gives a very reasonable and varied choice of foods for the costs paid and the staff welcome guests with a smile. The dining area is spotless and very well looked after by all the staff. The location of the hotel is perfect for us and where we want to go. Having visited the hotel many times now, we find our way around easily with the two tube stations so close by too. Thank you very much for another great stay - we missed out during the pandemic years - but we’ve no doubt that we’ll be back to see you again soon. Best wishes to all at the Phoenix Hotel.

All in all, I can really recommend the hotel and I will definitely book it for my next London visit again. Thank you and keep the good service.

title: Great experience
body: I had a great experience at the Phoenix Hotel in London for two nights. As a solo traveler, I had requested a Single room on an upper floor with an open view. While small as expected, I had enough space, a very clean room, and a lovely view over a little park. I appreciated the kettle and was able to sleep well in a quiet environment. The hotel is located on a quiet street yet close to many restaurants and shops. It was also lovely to be close to Kensington Gardens for lovely walks. The proximity of two Underground stations was most helpful to getting anywhere in the city, as well as easy travel to London Heathrow via the Elizabeth Line from Paddington Station for a flight. The cost was quite reasonable for London, and I chose to get breakfast on my own instead of the hotel breakfast, so can't comment on that. I wouldn't hesitate to choose Phoenix Hotel on future travels to London.

title: Great hotel if you don't mind a little noise from the rooms next door. :)
body: Had a really good stay at the hotel for six nights in May. The room while compact was big enough for all my needs, the building was clean, and the continental breakfast that came included because I booked direct with the hotel was delicious. The hotel itself is a short walk away from Bayswater tube station on the circle and district lines, and Queensway on the central line is just a little further down the same road, so plenty of transport options close at hand. I will admit I was slightly frustrated by how easily I could hear the people in the room beside and across the hall from mine through the thin walls since I was trying to work remotely on my laptop from my room in the evenings, but I understand it's an old building and those sorts of soundproofing issues are beyond anyone's reasonable control. It was a minor issue, but absolutely not enough to prevent me from having a good stay. I'd certainly recommend the hotel to anyone wanting to stay in the Bayswater area so long as they didn't mind a little noise from their neighbours. :)

It is close to Kensington Gardens and two Underground stops and the local high street has plenty of shops and nice restaurants. I have stayed at the hotel twice and recommend it. My room was comfortable and quiet during the night.

title: Overall a good stay.
body: Rooms were clean though small, but not uncommon or unexpected for Europe. Breakfast was pretty good (cold selections of ham & turkey slices, cheeses, yogurt, fruit, breads & pastries, croissants, jams, cereals, a few salad items, juices, coffee machine. Beds were not uncomfortable. Location was good (with 5-6 minutes of 2 Tube stations & a couple bus routes). Several restaurants walkable. Walking distance from Kensington Gardens & Notting Hill.
